landscapeSurvivors.section: W3 — The showcase, rebuilt to the wow bar
landscapeSurvivors.claim: Export pages enumeration and coverage acceptance criteria missing
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W3.2 requires 'Express ALL export pages' but the plan does not enumerate which pages exist in the design system export file. The acceptance criteria for W3 (section 'Acceptance: coverage matrix 100% or each gap owner-accepted') refers to the feature-coverage matrix defined in W3.4, which explicitly covers 'every W0.1 census feature' (kit features), not pages from the design export. Only three example pages are named: Identity Switchboard, Identity White-Labelling, Example Front Pages. No acceptance criterion states 'all N export pages are demonstrated in the showcase' or links page coverage to the coverage matrix.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Add to W3.4 acceptance criteria an explicit statement like 'coverage matrix includes all export pages from the design system export file enumerated in W0; each page demonstrated or explicitly deferred with owner acceptance.' Alternatively, clarify in W3.2 which specific export pages must be expressed, or create an acceptance criterion in W0 (perhaps W0.3 Demos Charter) that enumerates all export pages and confirms their assignment to demo apps with a citation in the coverage matrix.

verdict.reason: Confirmed first-hand against the plan file at commit 6f3221e1e (full text read, W0/W1/W2/W3 sections and acceptance bullets) and against the actual export directory (packages/design/design-import/claude-design/Oak Open Curriculum Design System/, mirrored at packages/design/oak-design-system/). The export contains ~80 distinct page-level HTML files: 3 top-level pages (Identity Switchboard, Identity White-Labelling, Example Front Pages), ~65 files under preview/ (buttons, colors-*, spacing, radii, motion, type-*, tabs, modal, a11y-charter, etc.), plus templates/lesson-deck, templates/worksheet, ui_kits/oak/index.html, whitelabel/creature/{index,card}, whitelabel/freedonia/{index,card}, whitelabel/specimen.html, integrations/revealjs, docs/headless-a11y-frameworks.html, and thumbnail.html. W3.2 names only the 3 top-level pages under "Express ALL export pages," with no census or count backing the "ALL" claim. W3.4's feature-coverage matrix is explicitly scoped to "every W0.1 census feature" (kit features: tier-1/tier-2 tokens, component class library, themes, composition tokens, print/deck/worksheet targets — not a page inventory), and W3's other acceptance bullet, "fidelity register against the export with every divergence dispositioned," checks fidelity of pages that ARE demonstrated, not completeness of the page set. No acceptance criterion anywhere in W3 (or W0.1's census, which is feature-scoped not page-scoped) requires or checks that every export page is represented or explicitly deferred. This is a real gap against a verbatim, emphasized owner requirement (point 4: "including all pages from the design system export"), and it recreates the exact failure class the plan's own Quality-bar section says it is curing ("every prior gate was machine-checkable and nothing forced anyone to look") — nothing here is checkable. Severity corrected to "important": it does not block W0–W2 execution and is fixable by adding an explicit page census/enumeration item plus a page-coverage acceptance line before W3 lands, but left as-is it lets the showcase pass its own gates while still missing dozens of the export's compositional pages (templates, whitelabel demos, ui_kits index) that were never named or dispositioned.

landscapeSurvivors.claim: W1 off-horizontal design-input gate does not explicitly block W1.1/W1.3 story starts
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: The plan states W1.3 is 'Blocked only on the owner design-input gate (frontmatter),' and the gate section records: 'W1 off-horizontal design input... Scheduled by the executing seat when W1 opens; W1's other stories do not block on it.' This creates potential for W1.1 (Identity schema) to complete without waiting for off-horizontal token definitions, then W1.3 to backfill. No explicit acceptance criterion in W1 requires the schema to include off-horizontal token shape before W1.1 acceptance.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Clarify in W1.1 acceptance criteria: 'Identity schema includes token shapes for off-horizontal dimensions (rotation, tilt) with placeholder values pending W1.3 owner input, validated structurally but not functionally tested until W1.3 completes.' Or gate W1.1 acceptance on W1.3 completion with owner input.

verdict.reason:
Both quotes are verified verbatim in the plan at commit 6f3221e1e. Frontmatter owner_gates (lines 29-36): "W1 off-horizontal design input: ... Scheduled by the executing seat when W1 opens; W1's other stories do not block on it." W1.3 (lines 131-134): "Off-horizontal dimension: ... Blocked only on the owner design-input gate (frontmatter); scaffold the token shape first so the session prices real options." W1's acceptance line (140-143) reads only "schema validates all three live identities; the №N falsifier demonstrably fails on a framework-code touch...; matrix gate wired into `pnpm check`" — no clause ties off-horizontal token shape to W1.1's schema acceptance.

So the underlying facts are accurate: nothing in the plan text forces W1.1 (Identity schema) to include or wait for the off-horizontal token shape that W1.3 introduces, and only W1.3's own bullet — not an acceptance criterion — carries the "scaffold the token shape first" mitigation. This is a real gap in plan precision.

However the claimed severity is overstated. The plan already names the mitigation explicitly ("scaffold the token shape first so the session prices real options"), which is precisely the mechanism that avoids the rework scenario the reviewer worries about. W1.1's schema is explicitly designed to be data-extensible ("Adding a theme is data, not code"), so a later-arriving off-horizontal field is a natural extension, not a breaking backfill. No owner requirement is violated — Freedonia's off-horizontal grammar and Oak's zero value are still guaranteed by W1.3 and the W1.4 gate matrix regardless of story ordering. And the plan uses workstream-level (not per-story) acceptance criteria throughout, so this isn't a special omission unique to W1.1/W1.3 — it's the document's uniform granularity. This reads as a minor plan-clarity nit (worth a one-line acceptance addition tying schema completeness to the off-horizontal shape) rather than a blocking or important structural defect.

This is a real, narrow, easily-fixable planning gap (not a structural flaw invalidating the whole document, and it doesn't block W0-W3/W4.1/W4.2 from proceeding independently), so I'm setting severity to "important" rather than "blocking."

landscapeSurvivors.claim: Charter citation requirement creates forward dependency beyond W0 gate closure
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W0 acceptance (line 119-120) requires 'charter...cited from all four demo READMEs (two exist, two are created in W4)'. Only two READMEs exist during W0; the other two are created in W4. W0 cannot verify full acceptance until W4.3 completes, making W0 gate closure impossible under stated criteria.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Revise W0 acceptance to: 'charter landed in demos/README.md; cited from two existing demo READMEs; remaining citations will be added when W4 READMEs are created (tracked forward dependency, not gate-blocking).' Record as handoff obligation.

verdict.reason:
The textual claim is accurate. Plan file (commit 6f3221e1e), W0 Acceptance line (lines 119-120): "Acceptance: census checklist committed; gates green with evidence; charter landed and cited from all four demo READMEs (two exist, two are created in W4)." Repo state confirms the parenthetical: only demos/oak-curriculum-hub/README.md and demos/oak-design-showcase/README.md exist today; demos/oak-plain-pages and demos/oak-styled-components (W4.1/W4.2) don't exist yet. So this W0 acceptance item, read literally, cannot be fully true until after W4 creates the other two READMEs and they cite the charter — a genuine forward reference embedded in an earlier workstream's acceptance line.

However, the severity the claim implies ("W0 cannot verify full acceptance until W4.3 completes, making W0 gate closure impossible") overstates the practical effect and should be corrected down to minor:

1. The parenthetical is the plan authors' own explicit disclosure of the two-exist/two-created-later split, not a hidden oversight the reviewer uncovered — it's documented in the same sentence.
2. Nothing in this plan or in the repo's plan schema (.agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md) establishes that a workstream's informal "Acceptance:" line is a hard, literal, all-clauses-true gate blocking the next workstream. The schema's actual required "Acceptance criteria (each with a proof)" construct applies at the whole-node level (this file uses informal per-workstream Acceptance lines instead, a separate, unrelated deviation from the template).
3. The plan's own Sequencing section explicitly permits parallelism that undercuts strict serial gating: "W4.1 may start after W0 ... W4.2 after W2" — so the two missing READMEs can come into existence well before W3 finishes, and nothing stops W1-W3 from proceeding in the interim.

Net: this is a real drafting imprecision worth a small rewording fix (e.g., scope the W0 clause to the two READMEs that exist at W0 close, and let W4's own acceptance carry the citation requirement for the READMEs it creates), not a defect that blocks or invalidates the plan's gate structure.

landscapeSurvivors.claim: Identity schema acceptance claims validation of 'live identities' before Freedonia design details exist
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W1 acceptance requires 'schema validates all three live identities' but frontmatter owner-decision gate makes Freedonia off-horizontal design input a separate gate (expires 2026-08-31) not blocking W1. Meaning W1 can complete without Freedonia design finalized. Term 'live identities' is ambiguous: schema-valid only, or finalized design values?
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Define W1 acceptance precisely: 'schema structure validated and Oak/EMC² values finalized; Freedonia scaffold complete, values pending design-input gate closure.' Current phrasing allows W1 sign-off with Freedonia TBD, risking assumptions about Freedonia completeness in W2/W3.

verdict.reason:
First-hand read of `.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md` at 6f3221e1e confirms the literal facts cited: W1's acceptance line reads exactly "schema validates all three live identities; the №N falsifier demonstrably fails on a framework-code touch (proven once, red-then-green); matrix gate wired into `pnpm check`." — the phrase "live identities" is not defined anywhere else in the document (single occurrence). The frontmatter's second owner_gates entry is exactly as described: awaiting owner-decision, "W1 off-horizontal design input... Scheduled by the executing seat when W1 opens; W1's other stories do not block on it," expires 2026-08-31 — textually separate from and non-blocking to W1's other stories. So the evidence offered is accurate as quoted.

However, the claimed defect is weaker than presented once the workstream structure is read as a whole. W1.1 ("Identity schema") defines the schema as "tokens + assets + voice + composition preferences + polarity default" — it does not include off-horizontal/tilt. Off-horizontal is scoped as its own separate item, W1.3, which explicitly says: "Blocked only on the owner design-input gate (frontmatter); scaffold the token shape first so the session prices real options." That is a deliberate, stated scaffold-now/values-later sequencing, not a silent gap: the plan already anticipates that the off-horizontal token *shape* can exist and validate before the owner supplies Freedonia's actual tilt values. Under that reading, "schema validates all three live identities" most naturally maps to the W1.1 base identity contract (which has no off-horizontal dependency), not to finalized Freedonia design values — narrowing, though not eliminating, the ambiguity.

More importantly, the plan carries downstream enforcement that would catch exactly the failure mode the claim worries about (Freedonia shipping visually indistinguishable from Oak because W1 "completed" on schema-validity alone): the W3 "Quality bar — the wow checkpoint" requires every demo/page to be rendered in the owner's Chrome and pass his verdict, and W3.4's feature-coverage matrix must be "100% or each gap owner-accepted." Point 9 (Freedonia more off-horizontal, Oak none) is squarely inside that checkpoint. So even if W1's acceptance line is read loosely, the plan does not let an under-differentiated Freedonia reach completion undetected.

Net: the ambiguity in the term "live identities" is real and worth a one-line clarification (e.g., explicitly scoping W1's acceptance to the base schema and treating W1.3's real-value completion as tracked separately), but it is a wording/documentation gap rather than a structural planning defect — the plan's own sequencing (scaffold-first, gate named and dated) and its later mechanical+owner-rendered gates already guard against the substantive risk. Downgrading from whatever severity was implied to minor.

landscapeSurvivors.claim: Export-tweaks blocking condition lacks surfacing mechanism
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W0.5 (line 116-117) states tweaks 'none block later workstreams unless the owner marks one blocking'. No section specifies: how seat learns which tweaks are blocking, who surfaces this, what tracking surface is used, when the decision is made. Policy exists but execution surface is missing.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Add to W0.5: 'Blocking-tweak intake: [channel/ticket] read by executing seat at [date/gate]. Owner's blocking decision recorded [surface] by [role] no later than [milestone]. Tweaks not marked blocking by [date] proceed non-blocking.' Commit a specific decision point before W1 starts.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed against .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md at commit 6f3221e1e. W0.5 (lines 115-117) reads: "Export-tweaks intake: open the owner's tweak list channel; tweaks route through the design-sync path (ADR-213); none block later workstreams unless the owner marks one blocking." Grepped the whole file for "tweak" — the only other mention is the in-scope list at line 68 ("the export-tweaks intake"); no other passage defines a tracking surface, a check-in moment, or an owner-to-seat notification path for a tweak that gets marked blocking.

Checked the two things the clause points to, first-hand: (1) ADR-213 (docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/213-design-system-integration-and-component-architecture.md) defines "design-sync" only as the studio<->repo incremental-sync discipline (line 62) — it has no "tweak list," no blocking-flag concept, and no owner-mark mechanism. (2) The repo's actual .design-sync/ directory (NOTES.md, conventions.md) has zero occurrences of "tweak" or "block." So "the owner's tweak list channel" is a term coined fresh in this plan with no defined referent anywhere in the repo — the reviewer's core claim (policy stated, no execution surface named: no tracking artefact, no rule for how a seat learns a given tweak is blocking, no timing for the check) is accurate.

Mitigating factor the reviewer didn't credit: the plan's own frontmatter demonstrates a standing, well-specified owner_gates schema (awaiting/clears_when/expires, lines 15-38) used twice in this same document for exactly this kind of owner-conditioned block, and the repo's general practice (owner-attention-at-action-moments, surface-user-decisions-as-questions, use-agent-comms-log) gives a plausible generic answer a competent executing seat would reach for. But W0.5 never wires the tweak-blocking case into that mechanism, so the gap is real, not fabricated — it just isn't unrecoverable, since a seat that hits an owner-marked-blocking tweak has an established generic pattern (a new owner_gate entry) to fall back on even though this plan node doesn't say so.

One citation imprecision: no heading literally reads "Gate Dependencies and Sequencing" — the nearest section is "Sequencing and PR discipline" (line 217) plus the owner_gates frontmatter block. This doesn't change the substance of the finding, only its section label.

Severity: not blocking — the default (tweaks never block) is safe and well-defined, and nothing in the plan's own execution is halted by the gap. But it is more than cosmetic: a concrete failure scenario exists (owner marks a tweak blocking via some out-of-band channel; no defined surface propagates that mark to the executing seat; a later workstream proceeds when it should have waited), so "important" fits better than "minor."

landscapeSurvivors.section: Motion Axis Scope and Matrix Coverage
landscapeSurvivors.claim: Motion axis handling undefined in W1.4 gate matrix and acceptance criteria
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W0.1 census mentions 'five themes + motion axis' suggesting motion is separate dimension. W1.4 builds 'Gate matrix: contrast + a11y per identity × theme × component' without mentioning motion. W1 acceptance says 'matrix gate wired into pnpm check' without clarifying motion inclusion. Standing requirement doesn't mention motion explicitly.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Clarify W1.4: 'Gate matrix dimensions: (identity × theme × component) × (contrast + a11y + motion-compliance)' or confirm motion is handled separately. Update W1 acceptance to enumerate motion as explicit matrix axis if required for cross-demo theme detection.

verdict.reason:
Checked commit 6f3221e1e's .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md directly. All four evidentiary quotes are accurate: (1) line 99, W0.1 census reads 'five themes + motion axis' — explicitly treating motion as an axis ORTHOGONAL to theme, not one of the five themes; (2) line 135, W1.4 reads 'Gate matrix: contrast + a11y per identity × theme × component in CI' — three declared matrix dimensions, motion is not a fourth; (3) lines 141-143, W1's acceptance line reads 'matrix gate wired into `pnpm check`' with no motion clause; (4) the owner's standing requirements as given in the task (light/dark/high-contrast non-negotiable, colour-safe default, etc.) do not name motion either. Given the census's own framing splits motion out from the theme axis, a matrix declared only as identity×theme×component genuinely omits it as a fourth dimension, and no other clause in the plan names a mechanical CI mechanism for verifying motion-preference handling. This is a real specification gap, not a misreading.

However it is materially mitigated, so 'blocking' would overstate it: motion is not absent from the plan overall — W2.3 requires prefers-reduced-motion detection+selection as part of the theme runtime contract, W3.2 requires 'full theme + motion switching' in the showcase, W3.3 requires motion content on the token-reference page, and the Cross-demo acceptance section (owner amendment, binds all four demos) explicitly requires 'reduced motion honoured.' Also plausible by design: the W1.4 matrix explicitly generalises 'the existing four-theme CONTRAST gate' (packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts), a computed-colour-value check structurally unlike verifying that animations are actually suppressed, so folding motion into that specific mechanical matrix isn't a natural fit without further design.

Net: verified real gap in how (or whether) the motion axis gets a mechanical/CI verification path, worth closing before or during W1.4 authoring, but not a blocker to ratifying or starting the plan given the strong owner-facing acceptance criterion already present at the cross-demo/DoD level.

landscapeSurvivors.section: Quality Bar Enforcement and DoD Process
landscapeSurvivors.claim: Wow-bar DoD gate lacks defined process, timing, and verdicts surface
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: §Quality bar establishes 'The owner's verdict is the gate' and 'checkpoint is a DoD line' but doesn't specify: when owner renders, what interface captures verdicts per page, how seat knows render is approved, what escalation path exists if owner unavailable, how verdicts are recorded in fidelity register. DoD is principle without operational definition.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Add to §Quality bar: 'Owner rendering process: W3/W4 PRs include [checklist] enumerating render checkpoints. Seat files render artifact by [date]. Owner records verdict [comment/label] on each. No merge until all verdicts posted and green. Verdicts conserved in fidelity register.' Define surface and timing explicitly.

verdict.reason:
Checked against the plan at commit 6f3221e1e (`.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md`, §"Quality bar — the wow checkpoint", lines 203–215, plus §Sequencing line 223 and §Review record lines 255–260).

The two quoted phrases are verbatim-accurate: "The owner's verdict is the gate" (line 206–207) and "the checkpoint is a DoD line, not advice" (line 213) both appear as claimed.

Of the five specific absences the reviewer lists, three hold up as real textual gaps and two are overstated or misdirected:

- **Verdict-capture interface** — genuinely absent. The plan names inputs feeding the checkpoint (Chrome render, fidelity register, vision-critique leg, mechanical gate matrix) but never names how the owner's "wow"/"not yet" call itself gets recorded or signalled back to the seat.
- **Approval signal to the seat** — genuinely absent. "A page failing the checkpoint iterates within its PR" implies pass unblocks merge, but no mechanism (PR approval, a card answer, a checklist tick) is named as the seat's cue that it passed.
- **Owner-unavailable escalation** — genuinely absent from this section and not covered by the repo's `ping-before-escalate.md` (which governs peer-agent liveness, not owner availability for a render verdict).

Two of the five are weaker than claimed:
- **"When owner renders"** is actually specified at a coarse but real level: "at each page/demo checkpoint" (line 205) and "Renders to the owner at every W3/W4 page landing" (line 223, §Sequencing). The reviewer's evidence omits this cross-reference, making the claim read stronger than the text supports.
- **"How verdicts are recorded in fidelity register"** conflates two distinct things the plan deliberately keeps parallel: the fidelity register tracks export-vs-implementation divergence dispositions (a separate, pre-existing mechanism per the `oak-fidelity-review` skill and prior handoff records), not the owner's subjective wow verdict. The plan never claims verdicts land in the register, so faulting it for not saying "how" is a misreading rather than a real gap.

Net: the underlying observation — the DoD gate names *that* the owner's verdict blocks merge but not the concrete signal/interface by which that verdict is captured, communicated to the seat, or escalated if the owner is unavailable — is real and worth a plan-refinement note. But it is not that "process is undefined": timing is stated, the gate's blocking nature is stated, and standing repo-wide conventions (`owner-attention-at-action-moments.md`'s "blocking asks are ALWAYS cards," the "render in Chrome, pixels are the done-test" practice already cited in the plan itself as "standing practice") already supply a default mechanism this plan can inherit without restating. Correcting severity down from what the evidence implies: this is a minor specification gap suitable for a short addition (naming the card-based verdict signal and an unavailable-owner fallback) rather than a structural defect blocking the plan.

landscapeSurvivors.claim: Demos Charter is normative but production phase spans W0 and W4
landscapeSurvivors.evidence: W0.3 produces 'Demos Charter (demos/README.md §Charter, normative)' but only as section of that file. W0 acceptance requires 'charter...cited from all four demo READMEs' but W4 creates the other two READMEs. Charter is a two-phase artifact: W0 produces partial version, W4 completes citations.
landscapeSurvivors.suggested_cure: Clarify W0 acceptance: 'Demos Charter section landed with assignment table for all four demos; charter references point to [future] W4 READMEs (tracked forward dependency).' Or separate Demos Charter into its own file finalized in W0, with demo READMEs citing it.

verdict.reason:
Checked against the plan at commit 6f3221e1e (.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md, lines 106-120). The reviewer's direct quotes are accurate verbatim: W0.3 reads 'The Demos Charter (`demos/README.md` §Charter, normative)' and W0's Acceptance line reads 'charter landed and cited from all four demo READMEs (two exist, two are created in W4)'. W4.1/W4.2 (lines 180-189) do create the plain-HTML and styled-components demos whose READMEs are the missing two. So the core fact holds: an acceptance criterion nested inside W0's own 'Acceptance' block cannot literally be satisfied until artifacts from W4 exist -- a genuine cross-workstream dependency embedded in a single workstream's exit criteria, which sits oddly against the plan's stated sequencing 'W0 -> W1 -> W2 -> W3' (W1 nominally starts once W0 'accepts').

One correction to the reviewer's framing: calling the Charter itself 'a two-phase artifact' where 'W0 produces partial version' overstates the case. The charter's actual content -- the assignment table with all four demo rows (hub/showcase/plain/styled) plus the provenance note -- is fully authored in W0.3; nothing about the document's substance is partial or gets added to in W4. What is deferred to W4 is not charter production but citation-coverage verification: two files that will reference the already-complete charter don't exist yet. So the two-phase thing is the cross-file citation check, not the charter artifact itself.

Severity: minor, not blocking. The plan already discloses the dependency transparently in the same sentence via the '(two exist, two are created in W4)' parenthetical -- it names a concrete, falsifiable completion point (W4.1/W4.2 landing) rather than a bare 'deferred' status, which is exactly the sequencing-optionality cure the estate's own plan-body-first-principles-check calls for. Sequencing text also explicitly allows W4.1 to start right after W0, so the gap self-resolves quickly rather than stalling until the end of the plan. No executing seat is likely to be confused or blocked by it; it's a minor precision/wording nit in how the W0 acceptance line is scoped, not a hidden contradiction.

expertFindings.claim: W3.3's "content GENERATED from the DTCG source so it cannot drift" is not achievable against the current export: most tokens have no determinable `$type`, so any generator must guess presentation by inspecting values — which DTCG 2025.10 explicitly forbids, and which reintroduces exactly the drift the clause promises to eliminate.
expertFindings.evidence: Counted across `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/`: `component.json` 68 of 74 leaves carry no `$type` (btn.min-h, btn.pad, gap.*, …); `semantic.light.json` 54 of 146 (motion.*, shadow.*, focus.ring, type.*); `primitives.json` 5 of 98 — including all three `font.family.*` tokens; `semantic.high-contrast.json` 6 (shadow.*, focus.ring). Zero group-level `$type` exists in any tree (checked every group in palette/primitives/semantic.light/component), so no ancestor supplies the type. DTCG 2025.10 §type resolution: the type resolves token → group → ancestor group, otherwise "Token becomes invalid", and "Tools MUST NOT attempt to guess the type of a token by inspecting the contents of its value". `dtcg/README.md` also states `$type` is "heuristic" and "composite values (shadows, font shorthands) omit it".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W0.2 story: make the export generator emit group-level `$type` at every root group and composite `$type` (shadow, typography, border, transition) where the spec defines one, plus a `validateTypeCompleteness` check in `design-tokens-core` that fails on any leaf with no resolvable type. Gate W3.3 on that check being green; state in W3.3 that the page dispatches on `$type` only, never on value shape or path prefix.

expertFindings.claim: The plan treats two DTCG trees as one "source", and they run in opposite generation directions; worse, making the token-reference page a shipped consumer of the export breaks a ratified ADR-213 constraint that the plan never mentions (Stage B / the dual-gate window).
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/README.md`: "generated from the CSS source of truth … The CSS is canonical; regenerate these files after any token change — do not hand-edit". `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/build-css.ts` builds CSS *from* hand-authored trees, and its `src/tokens/` holds only palette + semantic.light + semantic.dark + component (no high-contrast, no colour-safe). ADR-213 lines 105–110 and the 2026-07-20 amendment (lines 172–178), echoed in `oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts`'s header: the export trees are consumed "as a validator-consumer only … no shipped artefact derives from the dtcg trees until Stage B", and Stage B deletes the hand-authored trees, their manifest and their gate atomically. Stage B is unlanded (`docs/governance/design-token-practice.md` lines 28–31: "Until ADR-213's Stage B atomic switch lands … the DTCG trees described here remain the live mechanism"). So W3.3 reading the export ships from a validator-only source; reading the hand-authored trees renders 2 of the 5 themes and builds on a tree scheduled for deletion.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the exact tree W3.3 reads, and record Stage B as a dependency — either a W0 story that lands Stage B (its ADR-213 boundary conditions are already enumerated: re-root at `color.`/`semantic.`/`component.`, resolve dialect aliases, pre-compute expression values, schema-validate the manifest) or an owner-recorded exception permitting one shipped consumer during the window. Fix W0.1's census bullet to describe the two trees and their directions separately.

expertFindings.claim: "Themes per identity … the schema REQUIRES light, dark, and high-contrast" is unimplementable against the shipped theme and brand contracts: high-contrast and colour-safe are authored as Oak-palette overrides that outrank every identity override and reference primitives the brand contract declares private. Every identity collapses to Oak's palette in exactly the two themes the owner made non-negotiable.
expertFindings.evidence: `colors_and_type.css:598-599` and `:690-691` author the two themes as `[data-theme='x'], :root[data-theme='x']` — the second arm is specificity (0,2,0), beating an identity sheet's `:root` (0,1,0). Counted in those blocks: high-contrast = 71 declarations, 68 of them resolving to 10 distinct Oak tier-1 primitives (`--oak-black-true`, `--oak-navy120`, `--oak-hc-red/green/ink-*`, `--oak-lemon`); colour-safe = 12 declarations, all 12 on 6 `--oak-ci-*` primitives. `brand.css` STABILITY clause: "Tier-1 --oak-* primitives … are PRIVATE: do not override them", and its contract states outright that "The [data-theme=\"high-contrast\"] and [data-theme=\"colour-safe\"] themes keep working untouched" — i.e. identity is *designed* to be overridden there. `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/*.css` contains zero high-contrast or colour-safe handling; creature carries one ad-hoc `.oak-scope[data-theme='high-contrast']` block.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W1 story that parameterises the theme overlays over identity-supplied palette slots (theme roles reference an identity palette namespace, not `--oak-*`), and amend the brand.css contract accordingly through the ADR-213 design-sync path. Change W1's acceptance from "schema validates all three live identities" to "each identity renders its own high-contrast and colour-safe palettes, gate-proven".

expertFindings.section: W1.1 ("Adding a theme is data, not code")
expertFindings.claim: The claim is falsified by at least five closed, hand-maintained theme lists that no W1 story generalises, and W1.2's falsifier only tests identities — so nothing catches the theme case. Executing W1 as written yields identity config that can declare a theme no runtime can apply and no gate can validate.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:31` (`type OakThemeName = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' | 'high-contrast' | 'colour-safe'`) and `:48` (`const THEMES: OakThemeName[] = [...]`, with `:76` allowing only current members to reach `data-theme`); `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts:39` repeats the union; `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts` pins `DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES`, `THEME_GATE_LEVELS`, per-theme `SEMANTIC_ROOTS` and `EXPECTED_COMPARAND_SIZE`; the CSS theme blocks are hand-authored; `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx:18-24` hard-codes `THEME_LABELS`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a theme-№N falsifier alongside W1.2 (CI mints a test theme for a test identity from config only; a build touching any of the five lists fails), and a story that makes the theme roster a generated artefact consumed by the runtime, the React types, the gate expectations and the demo label maps.

expertFindings.claim: "A DTCG-shaped identity definition (tokens + assets + voice + composition preferences + polarity default)" is a category error against DTCG, and its stated acceptance — "schema validates all three live identities" — is unreachable because the live identities are largely non-token CSS.
expertFindings.evidence: DTCG 2025.10 base types are color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number; composites are strokeStyle, border, transition, shadow, gradient, typography — no asset/file, no prose/text, no polarity type; a leaf with no resolvable `$type` is invalid; and `$extensions` is specified for "optional meta-data that is not crucial to understanding that token's value", which load-bearing identity data is not. The live identities are CSS: `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` has 6 rule blocks of which 5 are non-`:root` (`[data-page='unit']`, `[data-page='proof']`, `.mast`, `.mast .oak-link`, `.headline`); `creature/brand-full.css` has 12 of which 11 are non-`:root`, including `.oak-scope .oak-btn:hover/:active`, `.oak-scope .oak-btn--secondary:hover/:active` and a `[data-theme='high-contrast']` block.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the artefact: a JSON-Schema identity manifest (assets, voice, polarity, composition, icon set, theme roster) that *references* a DTCG token file for the token block alone; plus a declared, bounded "identity CSS layer" with its own rule (permitted selector shapes, no component-internal selectors). Add a W1 story that re-expresses the existing non-`:root` identity CSS as composition/component tokens, and make W1 acceptance the count of identity CSS rules that survive outside the declared layer.

expertFindings.claim: "CI mints a test identity from config only" presupposes a config → brand-CSS/assets generator that no story in the plan creates and that does not exist in the repo. Without it the falsifier cannot be built, or is built as a trivially-passing check.
expertFindings.evidence: Identity is authored CSS today: `brand.css` is described in its own header as "the WHITE-LABEL OVERRIDE CONTRACT … Copy it, uncomment what you change, and load it AFTER styles.css"; the showcase ships static copies at `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/brands/{creature,freedonia}/brand.css`; `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` switches identity by swapping a `<link>` element. `packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/index.ts` exports only `flattenDesignTokens`, `emitCssVariables`, `createCssBlock`, `validateTierReferences` — no identity or brand emitter anywhere in the package.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit W1 story for the identity emitter (manifest → brand CSS + asset/icon manifest + theme roster), and rewrite W1.2 so the falsifier consumes that emitter: red-then-green proof is "identity №N added as one manifest file, zero diffs outside the identity directory".

expertFindings.claim: "Contrast + a11y per identity × theme × component in CI, generalising the existing four-theme contrast gate" is not a generalisation — the existing gate resolves DTCG trees, and identities have neither DTCG trees nor contrast manifests. As written the story will be sized as an extension and discovered mid-flight to be a new mechanism.
expertFindings.evidence: The existing gate (`oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts`) imports only Oak's `dtcg/palette.json`, four `semantic.*.json` and `dtcg/contrast-pairings.json`, and pins `EXPECTED_COMPARAND_SIZE` per composed theme. `find packages/design/oak-design-system -name '*contrast*'` returns only Oak's manifest, the high-contrast tree and `studio-source/preview/contrast-audit.html`; the whitelabel directories contain only `brand-a.css`, `brand-full.css`, `icons.css`, `logo.svg`, `BRAND.md`, `card.html`, `index.html`. Identity contrast is checked today only interactively — `studio-source/preview/contrast-audit.html:121-124` offers the brand sheets as dropdown options for in-browser computation.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the mechanism explicitly: either per-identity DTCG projections plus per-identity contrast manifests (then the pinned-count structures in `design-system-expectations.ts` become per-identity), or a browser-computed gate over rendered identity × theme pages. Size the W1.4 story against the chosen mechanism and record the pinned-expectation multiplication.

expertFindings.claim: Off-horizontal is attributed to the wrong identity relative to the landed definitions: Freedonia is the repo's maximally orthogonal identity and has zero tilt, while EMC²/creature is the one with rotations and diagonals. Executing W1.3 as written either contradicts the Freedonia brand definition or silently re-designs it, and the owner design-input gate will be primed with an inverted premise.
expertFindings.evidence: `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/BRAND.md`: "Sharp as cut paper: radius 0 on everything … Flat signature: every decorative shadow `none`", "a document tradition that acquired a website", rules/folios/ledger grammar. Grep for `rotate|skew|deg` across `freedonia/brand-full.css`, `brand-a.css`, `icons.css`: zero matches. By contrast `creature/BRAND.md` names "sticker rotations on shelf cards" and "candy tone-bands with DIAGONAL gradients"; `creature/brand-full.css:38,71,122,130` carry `linear-gradient(135deg/160deg)` and `creature/index.html:63,71` carry `transform: rotate(-1.5deg)` and `rotate(8deg)` — page-local and untokened.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Attach this evidence to the W1.3 owner-decision gate so the session prices a real choice. If Freedonia is to tilt, add a story to re-author `freedonia/BRAND.md` and its sheets through the ADR-213 design-sync path; in the same story tokenise creature's existing page-local rotations so the new dimension has at least one already-designed consumer.

expertFindings.claim: The plan scaffolds "rotation/tilt as tokened identity attributes" without an encoding decision, but DTCG has no angle type and the repo's tier detector will reject the obvious placements — so the scaffold will be authored twice.
expertFindings.evidence: DTCG 2025.10 supports color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number plus six composites; there is no angle/rotation type, and `dimension` admits px/rem only. `packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/index.ts` `getTokenTier` classifies any root segment other than `semantic`/`component` as palette, and `validateTokenReferenceDirection` then throws "Palette tokens must use raw values." on any reference — so a new `rotation.*` root cannot reference anything. Separately, a naive "Oak has no rotation" gate would fire on existing glyph mechanics: `components.css:637,685,842,847,899,903,908` use `rotate(45deg)`/`rotate(225deg)` for chevrons and carets.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Decide in W1.3: `$type: number` with a documented degrees convention, composed into `transform` at emission; the tokens live under `semantic.` (identity-overridable roles) and `component.` per the tier detector; Oak's value is a structural literal zero, and the gate asserts the *token values*, never the absence of `transform` in kit CSS.

expertFindings.claim: "The hub gains this where it lacks it — the one change the hub takes while otherwise staying as-is" states an unverified repository claim that is false at 6f3221e1e. Acting on it invites an unnecessary change to the one demo the owner ruled stays as-is.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/layout.tsx:34,47` reads `public/oak-theme.js` and inlines it as a raw pre-paint `<script>` (with `suppressHydrationWarning` noted at :41) — detection. `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx` provides selection over `oakThemeStore` from `@oaknational/oak-design-react`, offering all five themes (`light, dark, system, high-contrast, colour-safe` at :18-24) plus the motion axis (`system, reduced, full` at :25-29), with `ThemeSwitcher.test.tsx` beside it. `app/globals.css:9` also records that the raw-hex `@theme` mirror "is gone" and the hub maps `@theme inline` onto kit role tokens.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the clause with a verification story: assert the hub already satisfies the cross-demo criteria (pre-paint, persisted selection, five themes, motion, no flash) via its existing tests plus one rendered check, and open a change only if that assertion fails.

expertFindings.claim: The plan leaves the single largest tier-violation risk of the styled-components demo unruled: a `ThemeProvider` theme object holding token values. That is a parallel token system, and it cannot see `light-dark()` or `[data-theme]` scopes, so it would also break theme switching in the very demo whose acceptance is working theme detection and selection.
expertFindings.evidence: The plan's first-principles check names "`ThemeProvider` interop with CSS custom properties" as a vendor surface to verify but states no rule. ADR-148's invariant, carried forward by ADR-213 §2, is that secondary outputs are "projections of the token source, never a parallel token system". ADR-213 §2 also records that `light-dark()` resolves against `color-scheme`, not `[data-theme]`, and that a `[data-theme='dark'] { color-scheme: dark }` bridge rule is required where design-system CSS reaches a sandboxed view — a JS theme object bypasses both mechanisms.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a cross-demo criterion: no framework theme object may hold token values — a `ThemeProvider` value carries `var(--role)` references or nothing, and every styled component reads roles through `var()`. Add the `color-scheme` bridge to the W4.2 story's checklist, and make "zero literal token values in TS/JS" a mechanical check for the demo.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 / W0.2 (three identities at all times)
expertFindings.claim: Rendering three identities (or several themes) simultaneously means subtree theming, which lands on an open, explicitly unruled kit defect. W0.2's generic KNOWN-ISSUES triage does not name it, so W3 can reach the wow checkpoint with visibly wrong colours in two of the five themes.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md` item 14: "`:root`-declared aliases freeze under SUBTREE high-contrast / colour-safe theming … Affects `--border-accent`, `--bg-selected`, and the whole Oak-dialect alias block (`--surface-mint` …)", and it closes "What stays open here is only the alias-block breadth question … until ruled, avoid dialect aliases inside HC/colour-safe *subtrees*". Item 1 is also live for W4.1: `@import`-only stylesheets (`styles.css`) "parse to zero rules for pages served inside this project" — plain pages must link the four sheets directly.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Promote item 14 to a named W0.2 story with a required ruling (re-declare every dialect alias per theme block, or narrow the subtree contract), and make it an explicit predecessor of W3.2. Record item 1 in the W4.1 story's consumption path.

expertFindings.claim: Identity asset delivery is undecided and currently broken in the showcase: the two counter-identities depend on CDN icon fonts, and the showcase's identity payload omits their icon sheets entirely — so "three identities present at all times" is partial today and would remain so unless a story decides asset delivery.
expertFindings.evidence: `studio-source/whitelabel/creature/icons.css` opens with `@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Material+Symbols+Rounded…')`; `freedonia/icons.css` with `@import url('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/…')`. `KNOWN-ISSUES.md` item 3 records this as a known network dependency and item 4 adds Public Sans from Google Fonts for Freedonia. `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/brands/creature/` and `.../freedonia/` contain only `brand.css` and `brand-a.css` — no `icons.css`, no logo. ADR-148's delivery posture for MCP views is no CDN.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W1 story deciding identity asset delivery (vendor icon fonts/SVGs into the identity directory, offline-safe, licence notices beside them as the kit does for Lexend/Roboto Mono), make the icon set a required field of the identity manifest, and extend the showcase identity payload to carry icons and logo so each identity renders complete.

expertFindings.claim: The enumerated dimension list is narrower than the kit's actual token surface, and one listed dimension (iconography) has no DTCG representation at all — so the page can be "complete" against the plan while silently omitting whole token roots, which is the drift W3.3 exists to prevent.
expertFindings.evidence: Listed: colour, typography, spacing, radius, borders, shadows, motion, iconography, layers. Actual roots — `dtcg/semantic.light.json`: bg, border, color, control, ease, filter, focus, motion, scrim, shadow, state, surface, text, type; `dtcg/primitives.json`: border, font, layer, leading, measure, radius, size, space, tracking, weight. Unrepresented by the list: state, focus, filter, scrim, control/density, size (target and icon), measure, ease, leading/tracking/weight, and the composition tokens (`components.css:33-35` `--flow-columns`, `--flow-gap`, `--key-align`; `:1234-1263` `--main-areas`). `dtcg/README.md`: "Icon URL tokens (`--i-*` and the `--ic-*` roles, `oak-icons.css`) are deliberately not exported".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Derive the page's section list from the token tree's root groups at build time, with a check that fails when a root has no rendering treatment — so a new root cannot be silently unrepresented. Declare the iconography section as sourced from `icons.json`/`assets/icons/` with its own drift check, not from DTCG.

expertFindings.claim: W2.1 ("Ship the full component set in `oak-design-react`, mirroring the kit's class library … every W0.1 component class gains its component or a recorded rationale why not") is the exact shape ADR-213 §3 rejects as a settled standing rule. Executing it as written lands an architecture the estate's own ADR forbids, with no amendment.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/213-design-system-integration-and-component-system-architecture.md §3 Standing rules: "**Re-wrapping the class library in a framework component layer remains rejected** (it would fork the tier-3 contract). This question is settled here and is not re-litigated per widget." The 2026-07-23 amendment reaffirms it under "Stands unchanged": "the rejection of re-wrapping the _class library itself_ in a component layer therefore also stands", and defines the tier as "a **curated, owned React component tier** … components adopted from `studio-source/` **with ownership**" seeded by the four studio components (verified present: `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/components/{OakButton,OakTag,OakIcon,OakSubjectChip}`). `components.css` carries 102 distinct `.oak-*` selectors, most of them modifiers (`.oak-card--aqua`, `.oak-tag--mint`) and layout primitives (`.oak-stack`, `.oak-cluster`, `.oak-flow`, `.oak-canvas`), not component recipes. The plan cites ADR-213 nowhere and carries no amendment.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-write W2.1 as curated adoption on the ADR-213 shape: (a) a class→construct mapping rule stated in W0.1 (recipe class → component; modifier class → prop/variant union; layout primitive → composition component; utility → `className` passthrough only), (b) the coverage table records the mapping decision per class rather than a component per class, and (c) if the owner genuinely wants a 1:1 mirror, carry a dated ADR-213 §3 amendment with grounds inside this plan before W2 opens — an ADR contradiction discovered mid-execution is a stop.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 vs W2.2 — which layer paints
expertFindings.claim: The plan never decides whether the React tier's components paint via kit classes or via Tailwind utilities. W2.1 says components mirror "the kit's class library"; W2.2 says "The Tailwind mapping as first-class consumption (the showcase's engine)". Both cannot be the engine, and each branch has a different downstream cost the plan has not priced.
expertFindings.evidence: Verified: `packages/design/oak-design-system/docs/nextjs-theme-mapping.css` maps Tailwind's utility vocabulary onto role tokens only (`--color-ink: var(--text-primary)` …), i.e. it re-exposes tier-2 roles — it does not reproduce any component recipe. The recipes live in `components.css` (1350 lines, `.oak-btn`, `.oak-card`, `.oak-quiz-answer`, focus rings, state rules). The showcase today has no Tailwind at all (`demos/oak-design-showcase/package.json` has no tailwindcss dependency; `app/globals.css` header: "owner ruling 2026-07-29: no Tailwind, no PostCSS, no mapping layer — the kit's own classes and token roles ARE the styling vocabulary"). If tier components emit kit classes, Tailwind is decorative in the showcase and W2.2's "engine" claim is false; if they emit Tailwind utilities, the recipes are duplicated in a second vocabulary that the plain demo (W4.1) and the styled demo (W4.2) cannot consume.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a Decision-log row: components paint via kit component classes (tier-3 contract, shared by all four demos) and Tailwind's role-mapped utilities are used only for page/layout composition inside the showcase — plus a W3 exit check that no kit recipe is re-expressed as utilities. Restate W2.2 as "the Tailwind role mapping wired and demonstrated as the showcase's composition vocabulary", not "the engine".

expertFindings.section: W2 / W3.2 / W4.3 — identity runtime binding is unassigned
expertFindings.claim: Every workstream treats identity as build-time data (W1.1 schema, W1.2 falsifier), but the live identity binder is demo-local, hardcoded, and deliberately non-persistent. W3 turns a one-page showcase into a multi-page one; executed as written, identity resets to Oak on reload, deep link, and any full navigation — visible failure of "three identities present at all times" and of the wow bar.
expertFindings.evidence: `<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` holds a hardcoded `const IDENTITIES = ['oak','freedonia','creature'] as const`, resolves sheets by convention `/brands/${identity}/brand.css`, and its docblock states: "Identity deliberately does NOT persist across reloads: persistence would need a second pre-paint bootstrap to avoid a flash of Oak brand (the exact problem oak-theme.js solves for themes)." W3.2/W3.3 add Identity Switchboard, White-Labelling, Example Front Pages and the token-reference page, each needing the identity axis. W2 lists only theme runtime binding (W2.3); W4.3 defers identity to "showcase-only scope". W1.2's falsifier only checks that a mint "touches framework code" — a new identity would still require editing this demo-side union, so the falsifier passes while identity №4 is unreachable in the only demo that shows identities.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add W2.4 "identity runtime binding": a config-driven identity list (fed by W1.1's schema output, no hardcoded union), a layout-level provider so state survives client-side navigation, and a pre-paint identity bootstrap alongside `oak-theme.js` so reload/deep-link renders the chosen identity without a flash of Oak. Extend W1.2's falsifier to fail if minting identity №N requires editing any demo source.

expertFindings.claim: W2.3 requires the runtime binding to expose detection of `prefers-color-scheme`, `prefers-contrast` and `prefers-reduced-motion`. The landed store's contract deliberately exposes none of that, and adding it naively breaks React's server-snapshot rule. The plan states an outcome without stating the contract delta, so the seat will either re-open a settled design or hand-roll listeners per demo.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts` docblock: "The store deliberately carries NO contrast-media mirror … no exposed snapshot can change and a re-notification would always bail out of useSyncExternalStore", and the snapshot "is the CHOICE model, never the applied html attribute". `packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js` handles `prefers-contrast` in JS only (auto() + one change listener) and leaves colour-scheme and reduced-motion entirely to CSS (`light-dark()`, no attribute when 'system'). react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore: `getServerSnapshot` "must return the same exact data on initial client render as on the server", and `getSnapshot` must return cached/immutable values — "Always returning different objects causes infinite loops".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the delta in W2.3: (1) detection stays CSS-owned for styling — no React branch may select styles from media state; (2) if display of the *applied* theme is required, add an `applied()` accessor plus a matchMedia subscription inside the kit runtime and surface it as a separate scalar snapshot (never a composite object) with `getServerSnapshot` returning the neutral value; (3) state that any media-derived control state appears only post-hydration.

expertFindings.claim: The claim that one mechanism serves every demo fails at the notification boundary. The React adapter emits change notifications only for writes made through itself; the kit runtime has no subscribe. With four demos (one of them plain HTML writing directly to `window.oakTheme`), any write outside the React store leaves React controls stale.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts`: `emit()` is called only inside `createSetters`' `setTheme`/`setMotion`; `subscribe` maintains a local listener Set with no `storage` event and no runtime hook. `packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js` exposes `set/get/choice/themes/motion` and no subscribe/observer; its only listener is the internal `prefers-contrast` change handler. W4.1's plain demo is specified to use "`oak-theme.js` for detection and selection" — i.e. writes that bypass the store entirely; the same holds for a cross-tab change or any kit-shipped control.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Schedule a kit story (framework-neutral trunk, W0.2 or W2.3): add `oakTheme.subscribe(listener)` fired on every `set`/`motion.set` plus a `storage`-event bridge, and re-point the React adapter's `subscribe` at it, keeping `emit` only as a fallback. Then "one mechanism" is structural rather than per-consumer discipline.

expertFindings.claim: W4.2 is unimplementable against the tier as currently specified: `styled(Component)` requires the wrapped component to accept and apply `className`, and the seed components accept only a `style` prop. The plan also never says whether the styled demo consumes `oak-design-react` or forks its own components — which decides whether the accessibility audit cost is 1+N or 2N.
expertFindings.evidence: styled-components docs (styled-components.com/docs/advanced, fetched 2026-08-02) plus the Next.js App Router guide (nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/css-in-js, v16.2.12) confirm the `styled()` wrapper works by passing a generated class through `className`, and require `compiler: { styledComponents: true }` plus a `useServerInsertedHTML` registry client component. The seed components verified in-repo take no `className`: `studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx` signature is `({children, variant, size, iconLeft, iconRight, disabled, href, onClick, type, style})`; `OakTag.jsx` likewise ends at `style`. ADR-213 §3 records the "honest **1+N audit accounting**" rule for shared widgets — forking doubles the visual pass per surface.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to W2.1's acceptance a prop-API contract every tier component must satisfy: `className` accepted and merged after the kit classes, ref accepted as a prop (React 19), semantic element choice explicit (`as`/dedicated `Link` variant) rather than inferred, and no `style` prop. Add a Decision-log row stating whether W4.2 consumes the tier (preferred; then it is the tier's second consumer and proves the thinness claim) or forks, with the audit accounting stated either way.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 — adoption of the studio seed components
expertFindings.claim: The four seed components the ADR designates as the tier's seed are inline-style components that track hover, press and focus in React state. Adopting them without a stated rewrite lands code that violates the estate's own no-hardcoded-values instrument and replaces CSS state semantics with JS state — which breaks forced-colors, print, and the brand expression layer. W2 contains no conversion story.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx`: `const [hover, setHover] = React.useState(false); const [press, setPress] = React.useState(false); const [focus, setFocus] = React.useState(false);` with a `base` object of inline style declarations and variant maps selecting colours off `hover`/`disabled`. `OakTag.jsx` renders `` and an ``. The showcase bans exactly this: `demos/oak-design-showcase/eslint.config.ts` `no-restricted-syntax` on `JSXAttribute[name.name='style']` — "Inline styles cap what a brand's expression layer can transform (kit specimen HOOK-CLEAN CONTRACT)". `packages/design/oak-design-system/CLAUDE.md` requires the double focus ring on `:focus-visible` and forced-colors support, neither of which survives JS-tracked focus state.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit W2.1 story: adoption rewrites each seed to consume its kit class (`.oak-btn`, `.oak-tag`, …) with variants as props, deletes all `useState` hover/press/focus tracking in favour of `:hover`/`:active`/`:focus-visible`, and removes the `style` prop from the public API. Pin the equivalence with a fixtures-as-parity test against the kit markup (ADR-213 §3 already names that instrument).

expertFindings.claim: "The hub gains this where it lacks it — the one change the hub takes while otherwise staying as-is" is false as authored: the hub already has working pre-paint detection and full theme + motion selection through the shared store. A seat reading this clause will look for, or manufacture, a change that is not needed.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/layout.tsx` inlines the kit runtime pre-paint (`escapeInlineScript(readFileSync('public/oak-theme.js','utf8'))` in a raw `<head>` script, `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`). `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx` is `useSyncExternalStore` over `oakThemeStore` from `@oaknational/oak-design-react`, offering all five themes and all three motion modes ("the access themes (high-contrast, colour-safe) are not optional extras"), and it is mounted — `components/SiteFooter.tsx:19` renders `<ThemeSwitcher />`. Its own tests exist (`components/ThemeSwitcher.test.tsx`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the clause with the verified state and the real delta if any: the hub's remaining gap is that it renders no controls at all pre-hydration (server snapshot undefined) whereas the showcase renders a geometry-stable disabled shell — state whether convergence onto one shared control component is in scope, or record the hub's delta as zero.

expertFindings.claim: "Content GENERATED from the DTCG source so it cannot drift" plus "per-identity via the switcher" cannot both hold: the DTCG export covers the Oak base only, and the brand identities exist solely as CSS override sheets. The seat's natural route — reading `getComputedStyle` in an effect — is derived state in an effect, produces hydration-time emptiness, and must be run per identity × theme (15 combinations).
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/` contains palette, primitives, semantic.{light,dark,high-contrast,colour-safe}, component, contrast-pairings — no brand trees; `grep -l "freedonia\|creature" dtcg/` returns nothing. `dtcg/README.md`: "generated from the CSS source of truth … **The CSS is canonical; regenerate these files after any token change**". Brand overrides live in `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/brands/{creature,freedonia}/brand.css` and `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/*`. react.dev's effect guidance (synchronisation only, not derived state) plus `useSyncExternalStore`'s server-snapshot rule make the computed-style route a documented anti-pattern here.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make W3.3 consume W1.1's output rather than `dtcg/` directly: W1.1's identity schema must emit a per-identity token tree (generated from each brand.css, gated for orphans exactly as the theme overlays are), and W3.3 renders from that build-time data for all identity × theme cells. Add an explicit prohibition on runtime `getComputedStyle` as the value source, with a single computed-style *parity test* (not the page's data path) proving generated values match the rendered cascade.

expertFindings.claim: W3.2 enumerates three pages as "ALL export pages", but the export carries far more. Since W2.1's coverage target is census-driven and W3.4's matrix is the exit checklist, the under-enumeration silently shrinks both the component tier and the owner's requirement (4) ("including all pages from the design system export").
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand count in `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/` (and mirrored in `packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141/project/`): 3 top-level pages (Identity Switchboard, Identity White-Labelling, Example Front Pages) **plus** 62 `preview/*.html` pages (buttons, card, inputs, modal, tabs, tooltip, toast, pagination, quiz-*, breadcrumbs, composition-regions, a11y-charter, contrast-audit …), 4 component pages (`components/*/oak*.html`), 5 template pages under `iteration-pull-preservation-2026-07-23/templates/`, `templates/lesson-deck` + `templates/worksheet`, the reveal deck, and 5 whitelabel pages. W3.2 names only the 3.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Have W0.1 enumerate the export page set as a committed list, then set W3.2's target from that list with an explicit disposition per page (express / fold into a specimen surface / owner-accepted exclusion). Derive W2.1's component coverage from the same list so the tier is sized by evidence rather than by three page names.

expertFindings.section: W3.1 — deleting the current showcase page
expertFindings.claim: "Its plumbing assertions survive as tests, not as a page" is not executable as written: the assertions in question are page-bound end-to-end specs, and several encode hard-won behaviours (pre-hydration geometry, counter-brand load-then-swap) that a from-scratch rebuild will silently lose.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts` describes: region contract, theme choice + reload persistence, no-choice "Page default", OS contrast without claiming a choice, motion collapse, identity switching, "switching between counter-brands never shows the Oak base", and "pre-hydration shell geometry" parameterised by viewport width. `tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts` runs the identity × theme axe matrix, identity × system-theme matrix, focus-ring contrast on the switchboard and inverted footer, and 320px reflow. The behaviours they pin are documented in `components/Switchboard.tsx` (320px under-reservation; 737–742px re-wrap) and `components/useIdentity.ts` (load-then-swap with a generation counter, React 19 `<link precedence>` rejected on documented semantics).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Change W3.1 to: the rejected page's *markup* is deleted; the existing Playwright specs are re-pointed at the new surfaces and must stay green as the regression floor, and the switchboard's hydration-geometry and load-then-swap invariants move with the components into the tier (or into the layout-level provider) with their tests attached. List any spec deliberately dropped with its reason.

expertFindings.section: Cross-demo acceptance — "zero raw literals at point of use"
expertFindings.claim: Introducing Tailwind into the showcase opens a hole in the no-hardcoded-values instrument: neither half of it can see Tailwind arbitrary-value utilities in `className` strings, so the cross-demo acceptance criterion becomes unenforced exactly where the new consumption path lands.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/validate-authored-css.ts` walks only files ending `.css` ("Walks every authored .css file in the workspace"); the TSX half is a `no-restricted-syntax` ban on the `style` attribute and `<style>` element (`demos/oak-design-showcase/eslint.config.ts`). Neither sees `class="bg-[#123456] p-[7px] text-[13px]"`. Verified there is no Tailwind-aware lint rule in the repo: grep for "tailwind" across `packages/core/oak-eslint/src` and `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/eslint.config.ts` returns nothing.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W2.2 story: an ESLint check failing any JSX class string containing an arbitrary-value utility (`-\[` pattern) in the Tailwind-consuming demos, plus a positive check that colour/spacing utilities resolve to mapped role names. Land it in the same PR that adds Tailwind to the showcase, so the gate never lags the consumption path.

expertFindings.claim: The plan states no `'use client'` policy for the tier or for the rebuilt multi-page showcase. With a layout-level provider for identity plus interactive components, the default path a seat takes is a client boundary at the root, converting the whole showcase to client rendering and undermining the pre-paint/no-flash claims that depend on server-emitted HTML.
expertFindings.evidence: react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client: the directive marks the boundary and everything imported below it becomes part of the client bundle. Today's showcase keeps the boundary low — `app/layout.tsx` and `app/page.tsx` are server components and only `components/Switchboard.tsx` / `useIdentity.ts` carry `'use client'`. W3.2/W3.3 add a persistent switcher across pages and a data-driven token-reference page; W4.2's styled-components tree is client by construction (Next.js CSS-in-JS guide: "The following libraries are supported in Client Components in the `app` directory").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the rule in W2's acceptance: presentational tier components ship without `'use client'`; only interactive residents carry it; providers accept `children` as a slot so server-rendered subtrees pass through unchanged. Add a W3 exit check that the showcase's page and layout modules remain server components.

expertFindings.claim: The hub has NO accessibility proof surface at all, and no workstream in the plan creates one — so the cross-demo criterion "WCAG 2.2 AA per the demos-tier standard" is unsatisfiable for one of the four demos as written.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/package.json declares no `test:a11y` (scripts: dev, build, clean, start, type-check, lint, test, tool:*); `find . -name playwright*.config.ts` returns only apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http (2) and demos/oak-design-showcase. Root `check` and .github/workflows/ci.yml:230 both run `turbo run ... test:a11y`, so the hub contributes zero cells. demos/README.md states the tier is held to "WCAG 2.2 AA". The hub is a multi-route app (app/course, /lesson, /curriculum, /rubrics, /standards, /wiki) with a disclosure-based MobileHubNav and search results — none of it axe-tested.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit W0 story "hub a11y proof surface": playwright.config.ts + `test:a11y` over the hub's routes and interactive chrome (SiteNav sticky header, MobileHubNav disclosure, HubSearch, ResultCards, lesson pages) across the theme cells the hub offers, and make it a W0.2 stabilise exit criterion. "Stays as-is" governs the hub's visual design, not its absent gate.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §Cross-demo acceptance ("high-contrast and colour-safe reachable", "OS signals respected pre-paint")
expertFindings.claim: The single theme mechanism the plan mandates for all four demos silently drops the OS high-contrast route for two large user classes: anyone who selects the "Match device"/system theme, and anyone without JS. There is no CSS-level `prefers-contrast` fallback anywhere in the kit, so honouring WCAG-relevant OS contrast preference is entirely JS-dependent.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js: `auto()` (lines 60-72) is the only `prefers-contrast: more` consumer; line 95 `apply(stored() || auto() || null)` short-circuits `auto()` whenever anything is stored — and 'system' IS a storable member of THEMES (line 26); the live listener (lines 99-104) bails on `if (!current && !stored())`. `grep -rn "prefers-contrast" packages/design --include="*.css"` returns nothing: colors_and_type.css keys high-contrast solely on `[data-theme='high-contrast']` (lines 598-599). demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx labels 'system' "Match device" — the user-facing promise is precisely OS-following.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make this a named W0.2 stabilise defect with a red-then-green cure: (a) add `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` CSS mapping to the high-contrast token block, scoped so an explicit non-system choice still wins, so the guarantee survives JS-off; (b) make the runtime consult `auto()` when the stored choice is 'system'. Add two cross-demo gate cells: stored 'system' + `emulateMedia({contrast:'more'})` → high-contrast applied; `javaScriptEnabled:false` + contrast 'more' → high-contrast applied.

expertFindings.claim: CSS-driven page re-ordering is demonstrated as a headline feature with zero acceptance criteria for reading order or focus order. SC 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A) and 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) are exactly what visual re-ordering breaks, and axe ships no rule for either — the mechanical matrix will stay green while the demo ships a keyboard-hostile page.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan §W3.4 requires "non-trivial composition re-ordering live"; §Cross-demo acceptance names only "keyboard-complete; visible focus". The composition mechanism is grid-template-areas driven (packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md item 7: maps under `[data-page=...]`, region→area assignment), i.e. visual position changes with DOM order fixed. demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts contains no focus-order assertion — only axe, ring contrast and 320px reflow.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to W3.4 acceptance: for every composition variant demonstrated, a scripted check that the sequential focus order matches visual order (walk Tab, compare `getBoundingClientRect()` top/left monotonicity) and that heading/landmark reading order remains meaningful. State in the Charter that a variant whose DOM order and visual order diverge is a defect to re-author in DOM order, not a feature to showcase.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §W1.2 (identity-№N falsifier) + §W1.4 ("generalising the existing four-theme contrast gate")
expertFindings.claim: The contrast gate cannot be "generalised" to identity × theme as written: it is a DTCG-token + hand-authored-pairings gate that exists only for the Oak identity. Counter-brands ship CSS-only `:root` overrides with no token trees, no pairings manifest and no per-theme blocks. As specified, W1.2's config-only identity mint would produce identities with zero contrast proof, and the owner-ratified per-theme gate LEVELS have no carrier in the new schema.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts imports only Oak trees (`@oaknational/oak-design-system/dtcg/semantic.{light,dark,high-contrast,colour-safe}.json` + palette + contrast-pairings). design-system-expectations.ts:21-28 pins THEME_GATE_LEVELS `'high-contrast': 'AAA'`, others 'AA', commented "Ratified gate level per theme (owner, 2026-07-20)". packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141/project/whitelabel/{freedonia,creature}/ contain only BRAND.md, brand-a.css, brand-full.css, icons.css, logo.svg, card.html, index.html — `grep -rn data-theme` across both returns nothing, and freedonia/brand-a.css has a single `:root {` token block.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: W1.1's identity schema must require per-identity semantic token trees per required theme plus a pairings manifest (inheriting the base manifest by default), and W1.2's falsifier must additionally assert that the minted identity is automatically contrast-gated across all required themes at the ratified levels (high-contrast at AAA). No identity may be mintable without contrast coverage; that is the accessibility half of "trivially arbitrary identities".

expertFindings.claim: The triage disposition set admits "accept-with-record" and "defer" for entries that are live WCAG failures, contradicting ADR-147 zero-tolerance; and one of those entries is a hard prerequisite for W3.2's three-identity/theme rendering, not a deferrable nicety.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md item 13: dark body links on lemon bands measure "4.48:1, gate-measured" — below SC 1.4.3 AA (4.5:1) — and pass CI only because that pairing is absent from dtcg/contrast-pairings.json (closed-list blindness). Item 14: `:root`-declared aliases freeze under SUBTREE high-contrast/colour-safe theming, with the standing instruction "until ruled, avoid dialect aliases inside HC/colour-safe subtrees". ADR-147 §Standard: "Tolerance: Zero — no skipRules, no accepted violations". The kit's own CLAUDE.md: "Every colour pairing at least 4.5:1 text ... in every theme".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W0.2 that accessibility-class KNOWN-ISSUES entries have exactly one disposition — fix — and add the missing dark-link-on-lemon pairing to dtcg/contrast-pairings.json so the gate measures what the register admits. Make item 14's open alias-breadth question an owner-ruled W1 prerequisite that lands before any HC/colour-safe subtree is rendered in W3.

expertFindings.claim: "Three identities at all times" is ambiguous between simultaneous on-page rendering and always-reachable switching, and the simultaneous reading is not supported by the current brand contract — brand tokens are document-scoped, so simultaneous rendering means subtree theming, which KNOWN-ISSUES 14 says is broken for high-contrast and colour-safe. Executing the simultaneous reading as written ships unaudited colour in the two access themes.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141/project/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-a.css declares tokens in a single `:root {` block (one `:root` occurrence, no `[data-...]` scoping). demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts `applyIdentity` swaps a single document-level `link[data-oak-brand]` and waits for it to join `document.styleSheets` — one identity at a time by construction. KNOWN-ISSUES 14 restricts dialect aliases inside HC/colour-safe subtrees.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Resolve the reading in the Charter. If simultaneous: add a W1 story to scope brand tokens under a subtree selector with per-theme overrides re-declared inside it, fix KNOWN-ISSUES 14 first, and run the gate matrix on subtree cells (not just root cells). If sequential: reword to "all three identities reachable at all times from the switchboard", so the matrix gate and the owner's point-8 mean the same thing.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §Cross-demo acceptance ("WCAG 2.2 AA per the demos-tier standard; keyboard-complete; visible focus")
expertFindings.claim: The cross-demo acceptance line under-specifies WCAG 2.2 AA relative to both the estate's existing proofs and the kit's own standing commitments. Two brand-new demos built to the literal criteria will ship below the bar the current showcase already meets.
expertFindings.evidence: Absent from the criteria but present in today's proofs or the kit's contract: forced-colours mode (demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts 'forced-colors keeps the page renderable @a11y', and docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md §Contrast rules under forced colours mandates its matchMedia-gated pattern for "Any forced-colours project added elsewhere in the estate"); SC 1.4.10 reflow at 320px (same suite, per identity) and 400% zoom (kit CLAUDE.md); SC 2.5.8 target size, where the kit's floor is "at least 44px (md 48px)" against WCAG's 24×24; SC 2.4.1 skip links (kit ships `.oak-skip-link`, components.css:1049); SC 3.1.1 lang; SC 1.4.12 text spacing.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Turn the demos-tier a11y DoD into an enumerated criterion list in the W0.3 Charter and require every demo's suite to carry: a forced-colours cell using the practice doc's matchMedia gate + self-retiring assertion, 320px reflow and 400% zoom, target-size measurement at the kit's 44px floor, skip link, `lang`, and text-spacing. Each new demo cites the list rather than the two-word summary.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §W3.1 ("Its plumbing assertions survive as tests, not as a page")
expertFindings.claim: Deleting the rejected showcase page deletes the estate's only browser-level instruments for the WCAG criteria axe cannot measure. "Plumbing assertions survive" names no a11y instrument, so the rebuild can land with a green matrix and materially less coverage than today.
expertFindings.evidence: Instruments that exist only in that workspace: demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/focus-ring-contrast.ts + the `expectRingContrast` legs ("axe ships no focus-indicator-contrast rule" — SC 1.4.11 ring-vs-surface measurement, including the cure for a hand-measured 1.12:1 instance on the inverted footer band); the 320px reflow probe with its minLeft check; the forced-colors cell; and tests/apply-state.ts `measureSwitchboardGeometry(..., javaScriptEnabled:false)` — the only JS-disabled shell proof in the estate.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W3.1 acceptance line: "no accessibility instrument is deleted, only re-pointed", with a named inventory (ring-contrast tool, 320px reflow probe, forced-colours cell, JS-disabled shell, identity×theme axe matrix) and a red-then-green re-point recorded per instrument before the old page is removed.
