expertFindings.claim: The per-page definition of done has a vision-based design-review leg and a mechanical gate, but no manual accessibility review leg — which reproduces, in the accessibility dimension, exactly the class failure the section says it cures ("every prior gate was machine-checkable and nothing forced anyone to look").
expertFindings.evidence: §Quality bar item 2 names only "the fidelity register", "a vision-based design-review leg" and "the mechanical gate matrix green first". ADR-147 §Why Playwright + axe-core: "Manual review remains necessary for criteria that cannot be machine-verified"; docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md repeats it. The pages in scope carry APG widget patterns (export preview set includes modal.html, tabs.html, accordion.html, disclosure.html, tooltip.html, toast.html, quiz-*.html) whose keyboard and announcement behaviour axe cannot judge.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an accessibility-expert review-mode dispatch to the same checkpoint as the vision leg, per page and per demo, run before the render is shown to the owner; record its findings alongside the fidelity register so the a11y verdict is as visible as the visual one.

expertFindings.claim: The React tier ships "the full component set" with axe-per-component as its only accessibility acceptance. axe cannot verify the keyboard interaction models, focus management or announcement behaviour these widgets require, and component-scoped runs are structurally blind to the page-level criteria.
expertFindings.evidence: The class library to be mirrored includes APG-pattern widgets: packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141/project/preview/{modal,tabs,accordion,disclosure,tooltip,toast,pagination,select,choice-groups,step-cycle,quiz-answers,quiz-order-match,quiz-results}.html. Plan §W2 acceptance reads "component coverage table complete; tier consumed by W3 with zero component-local literals; a11y gate green per component".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Per interactive component require: the APG pattern named in the component doc, plus keyboard-model tests (roving tabindex and Arrow keys for tabs, Escape + focus trap + focus return for modal, aria-expanded/aria-controls for disclosure and accordion, role=status/live-region announcement for toast, hover+focus dismissal for tooltip per SC 1.4.13). Gate page-level criteria (heading order, landmark structure, reflow, SC 2.4.11 focus-not-obscured under the sticky header) at page level, not per component.

expertFindings.claim: The pre-paint criterion names no mechanism and no instrument, and the styled-components demo carries a first-paint hazard worse than a theme flash that the plan never states: without the Next App Router style registry, server-rendered HTML paints unstyled until hydration, which fails contrast, focus visibility and reading-order expectations for that whole frame.
expertFindings.evidence: Verified against the live Next.js 16.2.12 doc nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/css-in-js: styled-components@6 requires `compiler.styledComponents` plus a client-component registry using `ServerStyleSheet` + `useServerInsertedHTML` so "style rules are placed before any content that might use them"; the libraries are supported "in Client Components" only. The estate already solved the theme half with a raw inline `<head>` script — demos/oak-design-showcase/app/layout.tsx and demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/layout.tsx both note "A raw inline <head> script is the only shape that cannot flash ... next/script beforeInteractive does not block hydration". Today's suite proves post-hydration state (apply-state.ts waits for the Theme combobox to be enabled), not pre-paint.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the pre-paint mechanism per demo in the W0.3 Charter (raw inline head script for the three Next demos; parser-blocking `<script src>` in `<head>` for the plain demo) and name a mechanical proof for "no flash" (first-paint capture or a parse-time attribute assertion, plus a JS-disabled cell). Add the styled-components registry, with a no-unstyled-first-paint assertion, as an explicit W4.2 acceptance line rather than leaving it to the W4 vendor re-verification note.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §W1.1 ("Adding a theme is data, not code")
expertFindings.claim: Arbitrary themes as data contradicts the shipped runtime and CSS, and the accessibility consequence is specific: the OS-signal-to-theme binding is hard-coded to Oak's literal theme names, so a config-defined identity whose access theme is named anything else silently loses the automatic OS-contrast route while still satisfying the schema's "high-contrast required" clause.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/oak-theme.js:26 `const THEMES = ['light','dark','system','high-contrast','colour-safe']` (a closed literal union, mirrored in src/oak-theme.ts:31 and 48); `auto()` returns the literal string 'high-contrast' (line 66); colors_and_type.css keys every theme block on literal attribute values (`[data-theme='high-contrast']` 598-599, `[data-theme='colour-safe']` 690-691). Adding a theme therefore edits framework code and kit CSS — the exact touch W1.2's falsifier is meant to forbid.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Have the W1.1 schema carry per-theme OS-signal bindings (which theme answers `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, `prefers-contrast: more`, `forced-colors: active`) and have the runtime read the identity's declared theme list rather than a compiled-in union. Then "light, dark, high-contrast non-negotiable" is checkable as a schema obligation with a live OS-signal route, not as a naming coincidence.

expertFindings.section: .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md §W3.2/§W3.3 vs owner requirement 4 ("ALL pages from the design system export")
expertFindings.claim: W3.2 enumerates three export pages; the export ships 62 preview pages, three of which are the system's own accessibility surfaces. Omitting them drops the published guarantee/obligation split that the kit's contract treats as canonical, and drops the human-facing contrast instrument the kit tells consumers to validate with.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141/project/preview/ contains 62 HTML pages including a11y-charter.html ("The holistic commitment — what the system guarantees, and what every build must still do"), a11y-combinations.html ("Legal text-on-fill pairings, focus ring, hit targets") and contrast-audit.html. packages/design/oak-design-system/CLAUDE.md: "validate with `preview/contrast-audit.html`" and "`preview/a11y-charter.html` is the canonical split of what the system guarantees vs what every build must still do".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the accessibility trio explicitly in the W3 page inventory, and apply W3.3's generated-from-source rule to them: the charter's guarantee column and the contrast audit's numbers should render from the DTCG source and the gate's own report, so the published accessibility claims cannot drift from what CI measures.

expertFindings.claim: The off-horizontal token dimension is scoped purely as visual grammar with no accessibility constraints, and the owner design session is scheduled to price angles before those constraints exist — so the session can ratify options that later fail reflow, target-size or motion criteria.
expertFindings.evidence: §W1.3 defines the work as "rotation/tilt as tokened identity attributes" and asks the owner only "which elements tilt for Freedonia, at what angles, and where the personality lives". Rotation interacts directly with criteria the plan already owes: rotated boxes overflow horizontally and break the 320px reflow proof the showcase runs per identity (SC 1.4.10); a rotated control's hit area is not its bounding box (SC 2.5.8, kit floor 44px); animated tilt must collapse with the kit's token-level motion axis under `prefers-reduced-motion` (colors_and_type.css:504-520); tilted running text degrades readability for low-vision and dyslexic readers.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Scaffold the token shape with its constraints attached before the owner session: no tilt on text-bearing blocks above a bounded angle, tilt never applied to interactive targets unless the untransformed hit area still meets the kit's 44px floor, any animated tilt driven by the existing motion tokens so it collapses automatically, and the identity's 320px reflow cell re-run as part of the W1.4 matrix. Then the owner prices options that are already inside the accessibility envelope.

expertFindings.section: W3 — The showcase, rebuilt to the wow bar (W3.1)
expertFindings.claim: W3.1 ('Delete the current showcase page … Its plumbing assertions survive as tests, not as a page') is a standalone delete story that cannot land green: four existing test files describe that exact page, so the commit either lands a red tree (forbidden by the atomic-landing invariant) or deletes the description along with the page and lets W3.2's replacement arrive test-last — the audit-shaped outcome the plan is trying to cure.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/app/page.unit.test.tsx line 4 imports the page directly (`import ShowcasePage from './page';`); <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Switchboard.unit.test.tsx renders the page's switchboard; <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts asserts page-bound locators (`.oak-canvas > [data-region="…"]`, h1 name 'Oak Open Curriculum Design System', comboboxes 'Theme'/'Motion'); <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts runs the identity × theme axe matrix over the same page. `.agent/directives/tdd-as-design.md` §The Atomic Landing Invariant forbids a commit that ends with a failing test or with product code whose description arrives later.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Delete the W3.1 delete-story. Replace it with per-page migration landings: in one commit, rewrite the describing test at the affected scale to specify the NEW page (Playwright spec + unit test), add the React/Tailwind page that greens it, and remove the old markup — the sequence in docs/engineering/testing-tdd-recipes.md §Updating E2E Tests After Implementation and .agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §When Behaviour Changes. State explicitly which of the current assertions are retained verbatim, which are re-expressed against the new DOM, and which are dropped with a reason.

expertFindings.section: W1 — Identity and theme contract, gates (W1.2 identity-№N falsifier)
expertFindings.claim: The identity-№N falsifier as specified ('CI mints a test identity from config only; if the mint touches framework code, the build fails … proven once, red-then-green') cannot be red for the reason the strategic parent needs it to be red. A CI job that mints from config by construction never touches framework code (unfalsifiable, permanent green); implemented instead as 'the build fails when framework files change', it fires on every legitimate framework commit (permanent false positive). Neither shape detects the actual thesis failure — an identity whose requirements are not expressible in the schema.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W1.2 and its acceptance line ('the №N falsifier demonstrably fails on a framework-code touch (proven once, red-then-green)'); strategic node <repo>/.agent/plans/strategic/design-system-as-configured-framework.plan.md §Falsifiability states the real thesis failure as 'adding or modifying an identity requires framework-code changes'. A once-off human demonstration is not a standing guard: .agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §Prove the guard bites requires a gap-closing test to be shown biting by mutation, and the guard to remain in the suite.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-specify the falsifier as two standing, discriminating cases: (a) a synthetic identity fixture that lives outside the framework's importable tree and exercises EVERY census axis (colour, type, spacing, radius, shadow, motion, iconography, polarity default, rotation/off-horizontal, composition ordering, assets), rendered in the same identity × theme matrix as the live three — it goes red the moment an axis is unreachable from config; (b) schema-rejection fixtures (identity missing high-contrast, missing colour-safe default, unknown axis) proving the schema discriminates. Enforce thinness with the existing dependency-boundary mechanism (`validate-boundaries` in the root repo-validators chain) rather than a diff heuristic. Cite docs/engineering/testing-patterns.md §Discriminating Fixtures.

expertFindings.claim: 'Styling sourced solely from the design system … zero raw literals at point of use' is asserted for all four demos, but it is already false for the hub, which the same plan says stays as-is, and no existing or planned check can see the two syntaxes the criterion now has to cover (Tailwind arbitrary values, styled-components template literals). As written the criterion is either an unbudgeted mass refactor of the hub or an unenforced sentence.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand count in tracked hub source: 548 arbitrary-value class occurrences under <repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/{components,app}, top forms `text-[13px]` (40), `text-[15px]` (32), `tracking-[0.05em]` (12), `rounded-[14px]` (10), `border-[3px]` (11). The only literal guard walks CSS files only: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/validate-authored-css.ts line 37 (`entry.name.endsWith('.css')`), doc-comment 'Walks every authored .css file'. Plan §Direction point 5 and §Decision log: 'the hub STAYS as-is'.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the criterion per demo in the Demos Charter row: state the hub's literal debt as measured (cite the count), record it as accepted or give it its own remediation story with a budget; and, for the showcase and styled-components demos, land a class-string / template-literal literal detector as a pure function with literal fixtures in the same landing as the first demo that needs it — the existing precedent is <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.unit.test.ts (positive and negative cases per axis).

expertFindings.section: Cross-demo acceptance — 'The hub gains this where it lacks it'
expertFindings.claim: The hub's single stated change is misdiagnosed: it already has pre-paint theme detection and persisted selection. The story therefore has no available RED at the behaviour scale, and it names the wrong gap — what the hub actually lacks is any rendered-scale proof surface for those behaviours.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/layout.tsx line 34 inlines the kit runtime pre-paint (`escapeInlineScript(readFileSync('public/oak-theme.js','utf8'))`); <repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx offers all five themes plus the motion axis over `useSyncExternalStore` with localStorage-backed choice. Proof gap: the hub has no playwright.config.ts and no `test:ui`/`test:a11y` scripts (package.json scripts are dev/build/start/type-check/lint/test/tools only), and <repo>/demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/a11y-axe.test.tsx disables `color-contrast` because jsdom has no canvas.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the hub story as 'land the browser proof surface that describes the hub's existing theme detection and selection' — Playwright + axe under the four categories in .agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §Browser Proof Surfaces, wired as `test:ui`/`test:a11y` so turbo and CI run them (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 230). RED comes from the missing assertions, not from missing product behaviour; verify the current behaviour first-hand before writing the story.

expertFindings.claim: 'contrast + a11y per identity × theme × component in CI' names no matrix unit and no budget. Read literally against the kit's class library it is ~121 components × 3+ identities × 4 themes per demo, i.e. four figures of axe runs, and it grows with the 'trivially arbitrary' identity count — the gate would be either unbuildable or a CI-time hazard, and the plan gives the executing seat no ceiling to design against.
expertFindings.evidence: 121 unique class selectors in <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css. The gate the plan says it generalises is page-scale, not component-scale: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts loops IDENTITIES(3) × PALETTE_THEMES(4) = 12 axe cells plus 3 system cells and 3 reflow cells; the four-theme contrast gate it also references is in-process token-pair maths (<repo>/packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.integration.test.ts, DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES = light/dark/high-contrast/colour-safe).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the matrix unit explicitly: (i) token-pair contrast stays in-process per identity × theme (cheap, deterministic, scales with identities); (ii) rendered a11y runs over a specimen page per identity × theme that carries every component class once — keeping the browser cell count at identities × themes, not × components; (iii) record the expected cell count in the plan as the exit number so a silently shrinking matrix is visible. Cite the existing loop shape in showcase-a11y.spec.ts as the pattern to generalise.

expertFindings.section: W3.4 Feature-coverage matrix / W0.1 Feature census
expertFindings.claim: The coverage matrix is specified as a hand-maintained exit checklist over a hand-made census, and 'demonstrated on a named showcase surface' is a presence claim. Both drift silently and neither proves the feature renders correctly — the same failure mode the plan cures for the token page one bullet earlier.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W3.4 ('every W0.1 census feature demonstrated on a named showcase surface … The matrix is the workstream's exit checklist') against W3.3 ('content GENERATED from the DTCG source so it cannot drift'). Repo estate makes derivation available: the DTCG source ships in the export and `oak-design-tokens`, and the class library is enumerable from packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css (121 selectors). Estate doctrine: .agent/rules/validators-must-recompute-not-just-record.md.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Derive the census mechanically (token groups from the DTCG source, component classes from components.css) and make the matrix a generated artefact whose gate fails when (a) a census entry has no demonstrating surface and (b) a demonstrating surface carries no passing assertion id. Bind each matrix row to a named test (spec title or test id), so the exit check recomputes 'every feature has a green assertion' rather than recording a tick.

expertFindings.section: Workstreams (all) — missing describing surfaces and cycle decomposition
expertFindings.claim: No workstream names where its state is observable from a test, at what scale, or what the first RED is; acceptance is written per workstream, not per landing. W2.1 ('Ship the full component set … mirroring the kit's class library') is a single story over ~121 classes with acceptance 'component coverage table complete'. This is exactly the plan-author-time omission the foundational directive says causes scaffolding tests and test-last work.
expertFindings.evidence: .agent/directives/tdd-as-design.md §One State, One Describing Surface: 'The cure fires at plan-author time, not at test-review time: state the describing surface in one sentence before the cycle decomposition is settled, and tag each cycle's test boundary against it.' The plan's W0–W4 bullets carry no test-scale assignment; §Sequencing and PR discipline covers PR mechanics (bot identity, Copilot, review-round budget) but says nothing about the atomic-landing invariant or the mutation check.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add one line per story: describing surface (rendered page / kit stylesheet / schema validation output), test scale and file-naming (`*.unit.test.ts(x)`, `*.integration.test.ts`, Playwright spec), and the RED it starts from. Slice W2.1 by component family so each landing is one test+code pair. Add the atomic-landing invariant and .agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §Prove the guard bites to §Sequencing and PR discipline.

expertFindings.section: W4 — The plain and styled-components demos
expertFindings.claim: The two new demo workspaces are specified without a test contract: no naming taxonomy, no vitest config pattern, no obligation to wire browser tasks so CI reaches them, and no hermeticity requirement — yet both brands the demos must show load fonts and icons from third-party origins, which would put real network IO into PR CI.
expertFindings.evidence: Reachability and CI wiring: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 230 runs `turbo run test:e2e test:ui test:a11y test:widget`, so a Playwright spec in a workspace without `test:ui`/`test:a11y` scripts is unreachable. Hermeticity precedent: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts aborts cross-origin requests and fails loudly on unknown origins (`assertOnlyKnownExternalOrigins`, lines 63-103); the need is real per <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md items 3 and 4 (creature loads Material Symbols from Google Fonts, freedonia loads Bootstrap Icons from jsDelivr and Public Sans from Google Fonts). Copying existing precedent bakes in drift: the hub's vitest config uses a broad `**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` include with no `**/*.e2e.test.ts` exclude, against .agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §Canonical Vitest Configuration.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W4.0 line stating the new-workspace test contract: Pattern 1 config from `vitest.config.base.ts` (or Pattern 2 with the mandated e2e exclude), explicit `*.unit.test.ts` / `*.integration.test.ts` naming, Playwright specs wired to `test:ui` and `test:a11y` scripts, and the hermetic cross-origin interception helper reused from the showcase. Note in the plan that existing demo-tier naming drift is precedent, not licence (.agent/rules/… precedent-is-not-correctness).

expertFindings.section: Cross-demo acceptance — 'OS signals respected pre-paint (no flash of wrong theme)'
expertFindings.claim: 'No flash of wrong theme' is stated in a form no test can observe, so it will be discharged by eyeball or by an assertion that does not describe it. The estate already has the observable form of the claim; the plan should state that form, and it must state the extra case the styled-components demo introduces (CSS-in-JS style injection at SSR is a distinct flash mechanism from the kit's inline pre-paint script).
expertFindings.evidence: The existing observable shape: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts asserts `html` carries `data-theme='dark'` after reload (pre-paint bootstrap) and showcase-a11y.spec.ts asserts `data-theme='high-contrast'` under `emulateMedia({contrast:'more'})`. Neither samples paint; both describe the resolved attribute. The plan's W4.2 mentions styled-components 'wrappers where the engine needs them' with no proof obligation attached.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate the criterion as the mechanically observable claim: the resolved theme and motion attributes are present on the document element before first paint under each emulated OS signal, and survive reload; plus, for the styled-components demo, one case proving server-rendered styles arrive with the first HTML (no post-hydration restyle) using the same attribute-level assertions rather than a subjective flash judgement.

expertFindings.section: W1 acceptance — 'schema validates all three live identities'
expertFindings.claim: A green-only acceptance criterion: a schema that accepts everything satisfies it. Nothing in W1's acceptance forces the schema's non-negotiables (light, dark, high-contrast required; colour-safe default on) to bite.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W1.1 states the requirement ('the schema REQUIRES light, dark, and high-contrast and defaults colour-safe on') but W1's acceptance only requires validation of the three live identities. The estate's live theme set is four (DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES = light, dark, high-contrast, colour-safe in <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts line 15), so valid-only fixtures cannot distinguish a required-theme rule from no rule at all.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add rejection fixtures to the acceptance line: an identity missing high-contrast fails; an identity with colour-safe absent fails or defaults on observably; an identity declaring an unmodelled axis fails. Apply the mutation check (.agent/directives/testing-strategy.md §Prove the guard bites) to each before the landing that adds the schema.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 acceptance — 'three identities present at all times'
expertFindings.claim: The plan maps owner point 8 to a CI render matrix ('All three identities render across all themes in CI — the point-8 "at all times" as structure'). Rendering each identity in CI proves capability, not that every showcase surface continuously offers all three — the requirement as stated is about the surface, and no acceptance line describes it.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W1.4 and W3.2; the existing suite's identity assertions are switch-driven, not presence-driven (<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts exports IDENTITIES = ['oak','freedonia','creature'] and the specs call `applyIdentity` per case). The current page test asserts only that an Identity combobox exists (<repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/app/page.unit.test.tsx line 21).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add one assertion per showcase page that the identity control offers exactly the three configured identities, and that the set is unchanged after theme, motion and identity switches — a description of the surface requirement, alongside (not instead of) the render matrix.

expertFindings.claim: The PR-709 disposition transfers named test-bearing value ('appearance baselines, theme-control guards') into W2.3, W3.2 and the cross-demo criteria, but nothing binds those artefacts to a landing, so the transfer can be recorded as done while the guards are never re-authored.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan §PR-709: 'its adjudicated development-lane value — island hydration + ADR-217 amendment, appearance baselines, theme-control guards — transfers into W2.3, W3.2, and the cross-demo theme criteria … Commits remain reachable via the PR ref.' No workstream bullet names those artefacts; W2.3 and W3.2 make no reference to inherited baselines or guards.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Enumerate the transferring artefacts by file, and attach each to the specific story that must land it with its describing test; make the PR-709 closure comment list the destination story ids so the transfer is checkable rather than asserted.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — whole node (no §ADR obligations section)
expertFindings.claim: The plan names no ADR update obligation anywhere, yet at least three of its workstreams change surfaces that live ADRs currently describe. Executed as written it lands architecture that contradicts the ADR corpus with no dated amendment.
expertFindings.evidence: (1) `docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/041-workspace-structure-option-a.md:33-34` enumerates the tier by name — "`demos/` – demonstration apps consuming workspace package surfaces only (`oak-curriculum-hub`, `oak-design-showcase`)" — while W4.1/W4.2 create two more demo workspaces; the same ADR's `packages/design/` row two lines above carries the warning in its own words: "row trued 2026-08-02; the original two-name enumeration had gone stale by three", and the ADR-213 §3 landing sequence set the precedent ("At landing: ADR-041's workspace map gains the new package (dated, additive)"). (2) W1.1's identity schema ("a DTCG-shaped identity definition … validated at build … Adding a theme is data, not code") sits directly on top of ADR-213 §2's amended interchange contract ("The interchange is a per-consumer projection contract, not a normalised tree" plus the three declared projections), with no amendment named. (3) W1.4's "contrast + a11y per identity × theme × component in CI" generalises ADR-147, which as it actually reads says "**Themes**: Both light and dark themes must pass independently" (147-…md, §Standard) and whose gate position/coverage matrix is mirrored in ADR-121.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit §ADR obligations section listing, per workstream, the dated amendment it lands in the same change: ADR-041 demos row (W4), ADR-213 §2 (W1.1–W1.2 identity/theme layer), ADR-147 §Standard + ADR-121 coverage matrix (W1.4–W1.5). Make each amendment an acceptance line of the workstream that triggers it.

expertFindings.claim: W1.5 and W2.1 take over workstreams that a conserved-but-cited plan still owns, and ADR-213 §3 names that plan by name as the executor of its hard gate. The plan neither cites nor amends it, so the ADR's pointer and the older plan's todos go stale silently — the exact failure ADR-213 legislated against.
expertFindings.evidence: `.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/architecture-and-infrastructure/current/design-system-integration.plan.md` (header: "🟢 EXECUTING") carries `ws-gate-extension` (status pending — "ADR-147 gate extension per the RESOLVED owner ruling … CI promotion of test:a11y") and `ws-owned-component-tier` (status pending, `depends_on: [ws-gate-extension]`, Linear MCP-134), plus `ws-fixtures-parity` and `ws-hub-migration`. ADR-213 §3 cites it directly: "the first component export requires the ADR-147 gate extension (`ws-gate-extension` in the design-system-integration plan …) landed for that package", and the same section states the discipline: "The design-system-integration backlog plan's React-fencing and fixtures-parity clauses carry dated amendments in THIS change, so no live plan encodes the superseded architecture." The new node declares `depends_on: []` and never mentions the plan.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: In the landing change, add dated amendments to the backlog plan's `ws-gate-extension`, `ws-owned-component-tier` and `ws-fixtures-parity` todos re-homing them to this node, and update ADR-213 §3's executor pointer to name this node (or, better, name the outcome and drop the plan-name pointer). Record the relationship in this node's body so the two records cannot disagree.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — W0.3 The Demos Charter
expertFindings.claim: The Charter is specified as normative decision content inside `demos/README.md`, an index surface. That puts an architectural decision (which demo demonstrates which consumption path, and the reversal of a prior owner agreement) in a file whose job is to point, and it duplicates content the same file already carries.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-127 §5: "**Stable indexes** — READMEs and index surfaces are APIs: they point, they do not carry", and "**DRY** — duplicated content drifts like copy-paste code". `demos/README.md` §Projects already carries per-demo consumption descriptions (the showcase entry reads "consuming the kit the plain-CSS way … with no Tailwind and no mapping layer"), which the Charter table would restate and contradict. PDR-019's reusability test puts a decision every adopter would otherwise re-derive in an ADR, and PDR-019's 2026-04-21 amendment keeps the WHAT in the ADR with sequencing in the plan.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Home the assignment decision as a dated ADR-213 amendment (or a new ADR, per PDR-019) and reduce `demos/README.md` to a pointer plus a row-per-demo table whose rows are the demo's own-concern content; rewrite §Projects to point at the charter row instead of restating the consumption path.

expertFindings.claim: The provenance note attributes to ADR-213 a normalisation it does not record, and leaves the 2026-08-02 owner word with no resolvable home other than this plan — a permanent doc whose authority is a plan, on a surface no validator polices.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.3 requires "the provenance note (the lost original agreement, the drift ADR-213 normalised, the 2026-08-02 deliberate re-assignment)". ADR-213 nowhere records a prior agreement that any demo would be plain HTML/CSS; what it actually carries is §3 ("**Tailwind consumption** is a mapping, not an adapter … The hub's raw-hex block is replaced by this mapping in its convergence lane") and §4 ("Named convergence consumers: … `demos/oak-curriculum-hub` (its hex mirror is a parallel token system this decision exists to kill)"). PDR-105's durability axis is enforced by `agent-tools/src/validators/reference-direction/validate-reference-direction.ts`, whose `POLICED_ROOTS` are `.agent/practice-core`, `.agent/rules`, `.agent/directives`, `docs/architecture/architectural-decisions`, `docs/governance` — `demos/` is not policed, so a README citing a plan as authority fails silently.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Cite ADR-213 §3/§4 for exactly what they say; record the superseded agreement and the 2026-08-02 re-assignment in the ADR amendment proposed above; have the charter's provenance line cite that ADR section only.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — W0.3 acceptance; W3 (showcase re-assignment)
expertFindings.claim: Re-assigning the showcase from plain-CSS to React+Tailwind falsifies four landed permanent surfaces, and the plan's only doc obligation is "each demo README cites the charter row it implements" — the kit-side correction ADR-213 mandates is not named.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/docs/consuming-nextjs.md:3`: "Two working proofs live in the oak-open-curriculum-ecosystem monorepo: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub` (Next 16 + Tailwind v4 …) and `demos/oak-design-showcase` (the plain path — no Tailwind …)". `demos/oak-design-showcase/README.md` opens "plain-CSS kit consumption — no Tailwind, no PostCSS, no mapping layer"; its `package.json` description repeats it; `demos/README.md` §Projects and `docs/…/041-…md:33-34` both name it. ADR-213 §3 requires the kit-doc route explicitly: "(Feed this correction back into the system's `docs/consuming-nextjs.md` through the normal design-sync flow.)" — and the backlog plan's `ws-design-sync-corrections` is the standing sync-back lane.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add the correction set to W0.3/W3 acceptance by path: kit `docs/consuming-nextjs.md` (via the design-sync sync-back), showcase README + package.json description, `demos/README.md` §Projects, ADR-041 demos row — each landing in the change that flips the showcase's consumption path.

expertFindings.claim: The PR-709 disposition is factually stale on landing and mis-states where the residual obligation lives: it claims value transfers into demo workstreams that cannot discharge it, while ADR-217 records that tail as owned elsewhere and still live in code.
expertFindings.evidence: `gh pr view 709`: state CLOSED, closedAt 2026-08-02T20:13:37Z; the plan commit 6f3221e1e is dated 2026-08-02 21:10 — so "PR number 709 … CLOSES at this plan's landing" describes a past event as future. The "ADR-217 amendment" named as transferring value is already on main (`git log` for `217-server-rendered-html-in-the-mcp-app.md` → 3acc1e2f9, dated amendment 2026-07-31). The PR's own adjudication comment scopes the residue as "reference value for the UNBUILT restack tail (PRs 4–6 of the MCP-128 stack — island hydration + theme + the ADR-217 amendment …). That is development-lane work", and ADR-217 §1's amendment says that tail "is owned by MCP-448; until it lands, the code deliberately bakes static markup at build time" — the MCP app is outside this plan's declared scope.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate §PR-709 as a dated fact (closed 2026-08-02, comment link). Split the transfer: the demo-lane theme-runtime substance into W2.3/cross-demo criteria; the MCP-app island-hydration/theme-control tail named as remaining with MCP-448 under ADR-217 and routed, not absorbed.

expertFindings.claim: Both workstreams plan to consume `studio-source/` export pages, which triggers an ADR-213 §1 obligation the plan does not name: such files leave `studio-source/` and come under the full gate in the same change.
expertFindings.evidence: W4.1: "candidate shape: the export's three pages re-pointed at the live workspace kit, static markup, kit stylesheets". ADR-213 §1: "non-production Claude Design source material (specimens, proofs, reference build, templates, reference components, integration examples, proof pages) lives under `studio-source/`; quality-gate scope exemptions bind that path alone … A studio-source file that becomes consumed by product code moves out and under the full gate in the same change." The pages exist at `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/{Example Front Pages,Identity Switchboard,Identity White-Labelling}.html`, and `demos/README.md` puts demos under the full tier gate ("strict TypeScript, the full shared ESLint ruleset, TDD, and WCAG 2.2 AA").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to W4.1/W3.2 acceptance: any studio-source artefact a demo consumes moves out of `studio-source/` and under the demo tier's gate in the same PR, with its licensing-manifest row updated; if the demo re-authors rather than consumes, say so explicitly so the boundary rule reads as considered.

expertFindings.claim: "ALL export pages" is an undefined closure claim, and the plan's own enumeration covers three of a much larger set — so the coverage matrix can be 100% green against a definition that never met the owner requirement.
expertFindings.evidence: W3.2 says "Express ALL export pages via the React tier + Tailwind: Identity Switchboard …, Identity White-Labelling, Example Front Pages". First-hand inventory of `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/`: three top-level HTML pages, 63 files under `preview/`, `whitelabel/specimen.html`, plus `templates/{lesson-deck,worksheet}`, `ui_kits/oak`, `integrations/revealjs`. The owner requirement is "ALL pages from the design system export". The no-moving-targets rule's open-set clause binds here by its own terms: it applies to "plan proof clauses" and names "closed class-sets" and "'global'/'complete' audit-scope assertions" as closure-shaped.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make W0.1 define the page set by filesystem enumeration at a dated commit and disposition each member (demonstrate / covered-by-another-surface / owner-accepted gap); have W3.4's matrix derive its rows from that census artefact rather than a hand-typed list, so the count is read-time-derived and non-load-bearing.

expertFindings.claim: The clause "The hub gains this where it lacks it — the one change the hub takes while otherwise staying as-is" states a repository condition that is false; the hub already ships pre-paint detection and full five-theme plus motion selection.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/app/layout.tsx:34` reads the kit runtime (`const oakThemeSource = escapeInlineScript(readFileSync('public/oak-theme.js', 'utf8'))`) and line 47 renders it as a raw inline `<script>` in head; `demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx` drives theme and motion axes over `oakThemeStore` from `@oaknational/oak-design-react` with labels for light / dark / system / high-contrast / colour-safe, and is mounted via `components/SiteFooter.tsx:19`, rendered from `app/layout.tsx:53`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the clause with the verified baseline and reduce the hub's cross-demo obligation to a verification step (prove no flash-of-wrong-theme, persistence, forced-colors, reduced motion against the existing wiring), naming any specific axis found missing at that check rather than asserting absence now.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — Acceptance lines in W0–W4 and §Quality bar
expertFindings.claim: No acceptance criterion names the evidence class the plan-node schema requires, so the node does not meet its own type contract and the owner-held wow checkpoint has no recorded home.
expertFindings.evidence: `.agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md` §Per-type contracts → Delivery: "**Acceptance criteria — each with a proof, required.** A proof names its evidence class: `repo-safe` (a test, validator, or CI check — cite the instrument) or `owner-held` (an external console or dashboard — name who verifies and where it is recorded)." The plan's lines read "gates green with evidence", "coverage matrix 100% or each gap owner-accepted", "the wow checkpoint (§Quality bar) passed per page" — no class, no instrument cited, and §Quality bar names the verifier ("The owner's verdict is the gate") but not where the verdict is recorded.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Label every acceptance criterion `repo-safe` (naming the instrument — e.g. `pnpm repo-validators:check`, `test:a11y`, the identity-№N CI job) or `owner-held` (naming the owner as verifier and the PR/comment where the wow verdict is recorded).

expertFindings.claim: The node withholds its ratification stamp on a misreading of the ticket rule, leaving a plan that "governs no work" as the routing target for an execution seat; and the gate carries multi-paragraph decision narrative in frontmatter.
expertFindings.evidence: Frontmatter is `status: sketch`, `ratified_by/date/where: null`, with the gate stating the flip to ratified waits on the ticket mint. `.agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md` separates the two: the stamp is `ratified_by` + `ratified_date` + `ratified_where`, while the 2026-07-31 amendment binds the ticket obligation only "within subtrees the operator tracks … a subtree is anchored when its strategic node, or any plan serving it, names at least one ticket" — here both this node and `design-system-as-configured-framework` carry `tickets: []`, so the subtree is unanchored by construction and no ticket is owed. `.agent/plans/README.md`: "Every plan is born `sketch` and governs no work until it carries a complete owner-ratification stamp", while §Execution seat routes Corsair to begin at W0. The delivery contract also states "(PDR-018: narrative in the body, never frontmatter)"; `owner_gates[0].clears_when` runs ten lines of decision provenance.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Stamp `ratified` now with `ratified_where` pointing at the resolvable record of the 2026-08-02 owner word; keep the ticket-mint condition as a short external-input gate (`clears_when`: one sentence) and move its provenance narrative into the body's §Decision log.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — node name, overview, §Direction, W2.1, W3.4
expertFindings.claim: The plan's proof clauses are closure-shaped against sets that have already moved once today, which the authoring-time open-set clause explicitly binds for plans.
expertFindings.evidence: `.agent/rules/no-moving-targets-in-permanent-docs.md` §Authoring-Time Open-Set Clause: closure claims bind "any prose artefact that will be read against a living surface — reports, PR narratives and descriptions, plan proof clauses, audit appendices …", naming counts and closed class-sets as the failure shape, with the cure "state open sets as classes with dated exemplars" and "make counts and closure claims non-load-bearing by default". The node's name and overview hard-code "four demos" (the set grew two→four the same day by owner amendment), §Direction pins "the eleven-point mandate", W0.1 promises "every kit feature", W2.1 "the full component set", W3.4 "coverage matrix 100%".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the node by outcome rather than count; state the demo set as "one row per demo workspace under `demos/`" derived at read time; state census and component coverage as dated exemplars of an explicitly open set with the census artefact as the read-time source.

expertFindings.claim: The strategic node's `serves` edge is not supported by the node's own rationale, weakening the traceability spine the strategy README defines.
expertFindings.evidence: `docs/strategy/stream-mcp-app.md:35` defines APP-1 as "Meet teachers inside the assistants they already use. Bring Oak to where planning already happens, rather than building a destination." The node's §Why strategic argues reusability and the licensing split ("code MIT, content OGL, marks reserved … the reusability argument and the constraint-surface argument are one architecture seen from two sides"), which reads against TOOLS-2 ("Open by default. Openly licensed code over open data; no lock-in", `docs/strategy/stream-engineering-tools.md:40`). `docs/strategy/README.md`: "A plan resolves to exactly one choice, which rolls up to its stream and Oak goal … the spine reads upward for coherence."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Either re-point `serves` at the choice the node's own argument makes (TOOLS-2), or add one sentence to §Why strategic tracing identity-as-configuration to APP-1's advantage claim so the edge reads for coherence.

expertFindings.claim: W2.1 mandates the exact component shape ADR-213 §3 has a standing rejection of, and the plan schedules no ADR amendment to carry the owner's newer word.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan: "Ship the full component set in `oak-design-react`, mirroring the kit's class library (census-driven; every W0.1 component class gains its component or a recorded rationale why not)." ADR-213 §3 standing rules (docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/213-design-system-integration-and-component-architecture.md): "**Re-wrapping the class library in a framework component layer remains rejected** (it would fork the tier-3 contract). This question is settled here and is not re-litigated per widget", reaffirmed in the 2026-07-23 amendment's "Stands unchanged" list ("the rejection of re-wrapping the _class library itself_ in a component layer therefore also stands"), where the tier is defined as "a **curated, owned React component tier** … adopted from `studio-source/` **with ownership**" and "packages only ever at need". The plan mentions no ADR-213 amendment anywhere.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W2.0 story that lands a dated ADR-213 §3 amendment recording the owner's "full optional React component set" word as the superseding substance and re-stating the tier-3 invariant the rejection protected (components consume tier-3 tokens identically, no forked contract). In the same story carry the landing-sequence obligations ADR-213 attaches to the first component export and that W2 currently omits: the ADR-041 map/roster edit, the `.design-sync/conventions.md` "exports no React components" rewrite plus re-sync, and the fixtures-as-parity migration from `oak-design-system` into the tier package.

expertFindings.claim: A "DTCG-shaped identity definition … validated at build" inverts ADR-213 §2's ratified source-of-truth direction and creates a second authored token source; the plan also names no home package for it.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 §2: "The design system's CSS is the token source of truth; DTCG JSON trees are a **generated interchange projection** of it"; packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/README.md: "generated from the CSS source of truth … **The CSS is canonical; regenerate these files after any token change** — do not hand-edit." Identity data today is authored CSS only: packages/design/oak-design-system/brand.css and studio-source/whitelabel/{creature,freedonia}/brand-full.css. The plan's In-scope line says only "the kit and token packages under `packages/design/`" and never names which workspace owns the schema, its validator, or the emission direction.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the direction explicitly in W1.1: identity remains CSS-authored and the schema validates a *generated* identity projection (with the generator named), or land a dated ADR-213 §2 amendment admitting an authored identity tree. Name the owning workspace (`design-tokens-core` is the existing framework/validation home; the kit's public surface is built CSS + `oak-theme.js` + `dtcg/` and cannot host a zod/TS schema).

expertFindings.claim: "Per-identity via the switcher" plus "content GENERATED from the DTCG source" is not satisfiable against the actual export: the DTCG surface carries no identity data at all, and iconography is deliberately excluded from it.

expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-specify W3.3's generator source: either extract from the canonical CSS (the actual source of truth, and the only surface carrying identity overrides), or add an explicit identity→DTCG projection story with its own total-coverage check before W3.3 depends on it. Drop iconography from the generated set or record the separate asset-path mechanism that supplies it.

expertFindings.claim: The plan silently duplicates workstreams owned by a live EXECUTING plan, with no dependency edge, supersession, or dated amendment on either side.
expertFindings.evidence: .agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/architecture-and-infrastructure/current/design-system-integration.plan.md is "🟢 EXECUTING" and owns `ws-gate-extension` (the ADR-147 extension — the plan's W1.5, verbatim the same deliverable), `ws-owned-component-tier` (MCP-134 — the plan's W2), `ws-fixtures-parity`, `ws-stage-b-convergence`, and `ws-design-sync-corrections`, all `status: pending`. True the stale `ws-hub-migration` status while there.

expertFindings.claim: Stage B is not landed, the dual-token-source window is open with a standing prohibition on new consumers, and the plan neither names it nor records it as a deferral while adding two new consumers.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/tokens/{palette,component,semantic.light,semantic.dark}.json still exist — the hand-authored trees Stage B deletes. expertFindings.claim: The "zero raw literals at point of use" criterion has an instrument in exactly one of the four demos; the plan doubles the tier without re-homing the instrument.
expertFindings.evidence: demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/validate-authored-css.ts sets `workspaceRoot = join(dirname(...), '..')` — it walks only the showcase workspace. The other half of the instrument is the JSX rule set in demos/oak-design-showcase/eslint.config.ts (`selector: "JSXAttribute[name.name='style']"`); `grep -n 'JSXAttribute|style' demos/oak-curriculum-hub/eslint.config.ts` returns nothing. Both halves are invoked from root `repo-validators:check` as `pnpm --filter @oaknational/oak-design-showcase …`. The same inversion holds for the kit-copy guard: KIT_ASSET_COPIES in demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/kit-asset-parity.ts hand-traverses into the hub (`copy: '../oak-curriculum-hub/public/oak-theme.js'`), and apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/build-scripts/copy-oak-ds.ts is a third copier outside it.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W0 story that re-homes both instruments above the demos tier (design tier or root validators) with the demo roster derived from the workspace inventory rather than hand-listed, so a new demo is covered by construction. Sequence it before W4 creates workspaces.

expertFindings.claim: The styled-components consumption path is structurally invisible to both halves of the no-hardcoded-values instrument, so its cross-demo acceptance criterion is unprovable as written.
expertFindings.evidence: The CSS half walks files ending `.css` (validate-authored-css.ts `entry.name.endsWith('.css')`); the JSX half bans the `style` attribute and `<style>` elements. A styled-components tagged template (``styled.div`color: #fff` ``) is neither. The plan nonetheless asserts for all four demos: "Styling sourced solely from the design system through each demo's declared consumption path; zero raw literals at point of use."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the instrument in W4.2's acceptance and land it red-first: a lint rule over styled/css tagged templates reusing the existing pure classifier `findLiteralDesignValues` (demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts), plus the non-vacuity leg the CSS walker already models (zero templates scanned is a failure).

expertFindings.claim: Creating two workspaces has no plumbing or boundary story; the demos tier has no machine-checked inventory and no enforced inbound rule, and ADR-041 explicitly enumerates the current two demos.
expertFindings.evidence: pnpm-workspace.yaml lists demos individually (`demos/oak-curriculum-hub`, `demos/oak-design-showcase`) — there is no `demos/*` glob, unlike `packages/design/*`. ADR-041: "`demos/` – demonstration apps consuming workspace package surfaces only (`oak-curriculum-hub`, `oak-design-showcase`). Recorded intent: never imported by packages — no boundary rule enforces the inbound direction yet; enforcement lands at need, mirroring the design-inventory leg (row added 2026-08-02)." packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/validate-boundaries.ts machine-checks packages/libs, apps, packages/sdks, packages/design and agent-tools — demos are absent; `grep -rn demos packages/core/oak-eslint/src/` returns nothing; .dependency-cruiser.mjs has no packages→demos or cross-demo rule (rule names: no-core-to-*, no-libs-to-*, no-sdks-to-apps, …).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit W4.0 plumbing story: pnpm-workspace registration, a dated ADR-041 demos-row amendment, a demos inventory leg in validate-boundaries.ts (the "enforcement lands at need" trigger the ADR names — four demos is that need), depcruise `no-packages-to-demos` and `no-cross-demo` rules, and knip/prettier/markdownlint entries.

expertFindings.claim: Both stories consume `studio-source/` proof pages without invoking ADR-213 §1's move-out-under-gate mechanism or accounting for the design-sync estate that ships those pages.
expertFindings.evidence: The three pages are tracked at packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/{Example Front Pages,Identity Switchboard,Identity White-Labelling}.html and are gate-exempt: `'studio-source/**'` in packages/design/oak-design-system/eslint.config.ts, `'packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/'` in .dependency-cruiser.mjs, plus prettier/markdownlint excludes. ADR-213 §1: "A studio-source file that becomes consumed by product code moves out and under the full gate in the same change." The same three filenames are literal `shippedFromRepo` entries in .design-sync/estate.json, whose reconciliation contract deletes remote files lacking a repo counterpart.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State in W3.2/W4.1 which mechanism applies: demos author fresh markup against the kit (pages stay studio-source), or the pages move out under the full gate — and in the latter case the `.design-sync/estate.json` entries and their repo canonicals move in the same change, per the single-home rule.

expertFindings.claim: The falsifier is not mechanisable as stated: a build cannot observe that a data-only mint "touched framework code", and the red-then-green proof contradicts the gate's own description.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan: "CI mints a test identity from config only; if the mint touches framework code, the build fails" with acceptance "the №N falsifier demonstrably fails on a framework-code touch (proven once, red-then-green)". A mint that is config-only has no observable relation to framework-source edits at build time; proving the red arm requires editing framework code, which the gate as described does not observe.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate as two checkable legs: (a) a fixture identity living in a data-only directory, with a boundary rule (depcruise/eslint) asserting no framework module imports identity data and no identity data imports framework source; (b) the mint pipeline runs green over that fixture with a non-vacuity check. Define the red proof against the boundary rule (an illegal import), not against an unobservable "touch".

expertFindings.claim: The anti-drift claim rests on a consistency gate that covers only two of the four theme trees; the two extra themes the identity contract makes non-negotiable are unguarded.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-tokens/scripts/validate-design-system-consistency.ts reads `palette.json`, `primitives.json`, `component.json`, `semantic.light.json`, `semantic.dark.json` only; packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/ also contains `semantic.high-contrast.json` and `semantic.colour-safe.json`, and the mismatch type in src/design-system-consistency.ts is typed `theme: 'light' | 'dark'`. dtcg/README.md notes the same limitation for the contrast gate ("would need to run it against all four theme trees, not just light/dark"). W3.3 asserts generation "so it cannot drift".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W0.2 story extending the dtcg↔CSS consistency validator to all four theme trees (and pointing W1.4's matrix at the extended surface) before W3.3's generated page is claimed drift-proof.

expertFindings.claim: The stated disposition is already discharged and the named value-transfer targets cannot receive the value, because every file in that PR is outside the plan's declared scope.
expertFindings.evidence: `gh pr view 709`: state CLOSED, isDraft true, title "docs(design): retention surface — landing-page port, design-lane input"; its files are all under apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http (landing-page CSS/JS, `build-scripts/copy-oak-ds.ts`, visual-baseline config) plus .dependency-cruiser.mjs and .github/workflows/ci.yml. The plan says "#709 CLOSES at this plan's landing" and that its value — "island hydration + ADR-217 amendment, appearance baselines, theme-control guards" — "transfers into W2.3, W3.2, and the cross-demo theme criteria", all of which are scoped to `oak-design-react` and `demos/`; `apps/` appears nowhere in the In-scope list.

expertFindings.claim: The tilt-per-identity assignment contradicts the tracked identity corpus and leaves the third identity unspecified.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/creature/BRAND.md (EMC² — "Educate My Creature Too") declares rotation as ITS grammar: "candy tone-bands with DIAGONAL gradients … angled bevelled shadows (8px 10px + glow), sticker rotations on shelf cards"; freedonia/BRAND.md is the restraint identity ("a **document tradition that acquired a website** … authority is carried by restraint and permanence"). Neither brand CSS carries any rotation today (`grep -c 'rotate|--tilt|skew'` = 0 in both brand-full.css). W1.3 gives values for Freedonia and Oak only.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Put all three identities' tilt values on the owner design-input gate agenda (the gate already exists in frontmatter), and schedule the BRAND.md canonical updates in the same change — they are `shippedFromRepo` to the studio, so a divergence propagates.

expertFindings.claim: Acceptance criteria omit the evidence classes the delivery-node contract requires, so most acceptance lines are unfalsifiable as written.
expertFindings.evidence: .agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md, Delivery contract: "**Acceptance criteria — each with a proof, required.** A proof names its evidence class: `repo-safe` (a test, validator, or CI check — cite the instrument) or `owner-held` (an external console or dashboard — name who verifies and where it is recorded)." The plan's acceptance lines (e.g. "census checklist committed; gates green with evidence; charter landed and cited from all four demo READMEs", "component coverage table complete; tier consumed by W3 with zero component-local literals") name outcomes without an instrument or class.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Annotate each acceptance line with its class and instrument — e.g. `repo-safe: pnpm --filter … validate-authored-css`, `repo-safe: validate-boundaries demos inventory`, `owner-held: rendered checkpoint in the owner's Chrome, recorded at the PR` — which also gives the wow checkpoint a recorded home.

frameFindings.claim: The coverage-matrix logic structurally regenerates the rejected showcase's shape: 'every W0.1 census feature demonstrated on a named showcase surface' is the recipe for specimen-inventory pages, and the plan binds coverage surfaces to no design grammar.
frameFindings.evidence: The rejected page is exactly this shape — the live showcase is ButtonsSpecimen.tsx, TagsSpecimen.tsx, CardSpecimen.tsx, TypeSpecimen.tsx (demos/oak-design-showcase/components/). The export has only three pages; the census (five themes, motion axis, composition tokens, print/deck/worksheet targets, icons, fonts) will contain dozens of features with no export reference, so most coverage surfaces are NEW pages designed by an engineering process. W3.2's 'real lesson-page specimen' hints at the cure but W3.4's exit checklist is feature-per-surface, which a specimen grid satisfies at 100%.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add a normative composition clause to W3.4: coverage is demonstrated only inside realistic product-grade compositions in the export's own layout grammar (lesson pages, front pages, worksheets) — a surface whose primary content is the feature itself (a specimen grid) fails the matrix by definition. Name the small set of composed pages first, then map features onto them, not the reverse.

frameFindings.section: Quality bar — the wow checkpoint, item 2
frameFindings.claim: The sole pre-owner aesthetic instrument — the 'vision-based design-review leg' — is one unspecified line with no rubric, no reference corpus, no defined failure criterion, and no named reviewer, so it is precisely a gate that can pass while the demo looks mediocre.
frameFindings.evidence: Plan line: 'a vision-based design-review leg (screenshot critique against professional design craft) run before any render is shown'. Every mechanical gate in the plan (contrast matrix, №N falsifier, coverage matrix) is specified to red-green precision; the one gate that carries the wow bar for all non-export-derived surfaces has none. The plan's own diagnosis of the class failure — 'every prior gate was machine-checkable and nothing forced anyone to look' — is answered with a gate whose looking has no bar.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Specify the leg as an instrument in W0: a rubric derived from the export's own design language (type scale usage, spatial rhythm, hierarchy, colour discipline), side-by-side comparison against an owner-passed reference page, an adversarial 'would a professional designer reject this' framing, and an explicit fail state that blocks the render from reaching the owner. Calibrate it once against the export pages (which must pass) and the rejected showcase (which must fail) — red-then-green, like the №N falsifier.

frameFindings.claim: The decomposition is infrastructure-first (W0 census/schema → W1 gates → W2 full React tier → W3 pages), so the owner's first wow verdict arrives after three workstreams of sunk investment; if the aesthetic direction is wrong, the feedback is maximally late and expensive.
frameFindings.evidence: W3 is the first workstream that renders a page to the owner ('Renders to the owner at every W3/W4 page landing'). W4.1 — the export's three pages re-pointed at the live kit with zero build machinery — is the cheapest full-page wow test in the whole plan, yet it is sequenced as permitted-after-W0 rather than required-early.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Re-sequence for earliest wow signal: make W4.1 (or a single W3 export page as a vertical slice) a mandatory early checkpoint whose owner verdict lands before W2 completes. Its pass also calibrates the design-review instrument against a page the owner actually said wow to.

frameFindings.claim: Owner requirement 3 ('enumerate and implement what is missing') is mapped to a census of what EXISTS whose output is a demonstration checklist; no workstream performs a requirements-vs-kit gap analysis or owns implementing kit-level gaps (missing token dimensions, missing kit component classes, missing theme machinery).
frameFindings.evidence: W0.1: 'first-hand enumeration of every kit feature… Output: the coverage checklist W3 consumes.' W1 owns contract gaps and W2 owns the React tier, but a gap in the kit itself — e.g. a standing-requirement token dimension the DTCG source lacks, or a component class the export shows and the kit omits — has no discovering step and no implementing home. W0.2 covers broken, not absent.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add a gap-census output to W0.1 (kit-vs-standing-requirements and kit-vs-export deltas, not just an inventory) and name the workstream that implements each gap class — kit gaps are W0/W1 work, not silently absorbed into W3 demonstration.

frameFindings.claim: The hub is inside 'each and every demo' for the wow bar but the plan grants it 'stays as-is' with theme controls as 'the one change the hub takes' — an unresolved structural conflict that will surface mid-execution as either a silent wow exemption or an unplanned hub redesign.
frameFindings.evidence: Quality bar: 'every demo, every page'. Cross-demo acceptance: 'the one change the hub takes while otherwise staying as-is.' If the hub as rendered today fails the owner's wow verdict, the plan contains no lane for curing it and no recorded exemption either.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Resolve explicitly in the plan: the owner's 'as-is' ruling covers architecture (Tailwind-mapped, plain path elsewhere), not visual quality; the hub goes through the same wow checkpoint, and a fail opens scoped visual-cure work — or record an owner-worded wow exemption for the hub. Card it if neither reading is certain.

frameFindings.section: W0.4 / W1.3 / W3.2 — identity visual quality
frameFindings.claim: No workstream allocates design authorship to making EMC² and Freedonia visually excellent; the №N falsifier proves identities need no framework code, but nothing tests that a non-Oak identity looks like anything more than token-swapped Oak — and the showcase shows all three 'at all times', so a flat EMC² fails the wow verdict directly.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.4 censuses what differentiates the identities today; W1.3 gates Freedonia's off-horizontal grammar on an owner session; EMC² appears nowhere as a design task. The strategic kernel's falsifier ('adding an identity requires framework-code changes') is purely mechanical — an identity of mediocre config values passes it while failing the visual bar the same kernel states.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add an identity-design story (W1 or W3): each of the three identities gets deliberate visual authorship of its config values (palette, type voice, composition preferences, polarity, tilt grammar), each passing the design-review instrument in its own right — so identity-as-configuration is proven with three configurations worth configuring.

frameFindings.claim: Fidelity-to-export caps visual quality at the July-24 export's level, and the only channel for exceeding it (the export-tweaks intake) is default-non-blocking — so if the owner's strengthened 'amazing' bar exceeds the export's current state, the plan structurally deprioritises the very work that would meet it.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.5: 'none block later workstreams unless the owner marks one blocking.' Quality bar item 2 measures export-derived pages by 'the fidelity register against the export' — a page can be pixel-faithful to the export and still draw a not-amazing verdict, at which point the cure is an export/design change routed through a channel the plan marks non-blocking.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Note in the Quality bar that a wow-checkpoint failure on a fidelity-clean page automatically promotes the corresponding design change to blocking in the tweaks intake — the owner verdict, not the intake default, decides priority.

frameFindings.section: Sequencing and PR discipline / Quality bar item 3
frameFindings.claim: The review-round budget of THREE per PR and the wow DoD ('a page failing the checkpoint iterates within its PR') can collide: a page needing four-plus visual iterations hits tally-stop and routes to the Director, structurally stalling exactly the iteration loop the wow bar depends on.
frameFindings.evidence: Plan: 'review-round budget THREE with the tally-stop discipline at budget (PDR-132)' alongside 'a page failing the checkpoint iterates within its PR; the checkpoint is a DoD line'. Visual iteration under a design-literate eye routinely exceeds three rounds; the plan does not say whether owner wow iterations count against the review budget.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: State that owner wow-checkpoint iterations are a distinct loop that does not consume PDR-132 review rounds (or give W3/W4 page PRs an explicit larger visual-iteration budget), so the budget discipline cannot become a pressure to land below the bar.
